articles.standfirst: Segundo a Gol Linhas Aéreas, o aumento do combustível motivou encerramento da rota. Companhia também anunciou descontinudade dos voos diretos para Manaus em fevereiro de 2027.
articles.summary: Segundo a Gol Linhas Aéreas, o aumento do combustível motivou encerramento da rota. Companhia também anunciou descontinudade dos voos diretos para Manaus em fevereiro de 2027.
articles.body:
Gol Linhas Aéreas vai encerrar os voos diretos entre Rio Branco e Porto Velho — Foto: Mendes Júnior/Arquivo pessoal

✈️A Gol Linhas Aéreas deve encerrar a operação de voos diretos entre Rio Branco e Porto Velho , em Rondônia, após pouco mais de dois meses do retorno da rota . A informação foi confirmada ao g1 pela empresa, que disse que o último voo da rota deve ocorrer durante o mês de novembro , sem data exata.

A companhia afirmou que também haverá a descontinuidade da rota entre Rio Branco e Manaus (AM) a partir de fevereiro de 2027 . As datas de encerramento são definidas com base na quantidade de passagens já vendidas.

O consultor de comunicação da Gol, Artur de Andrade, explicou que está revisando sua malha aérea em meio ao aumento dos custos com combustível. A empresa, no entanto, não descartou a possibilidade de retorno das rotas conforme demanda.

"A descontinuação da rota ocorrre em razão dos aumentos sucessivos do preço do combustível de aviação (QAV), que dobrou e representa cerca de 40% dos custos operacionais da Companhia, a Gol está ajustando rotas, com redução e/ou suspensão da operação em alguns trechos", declarou.

O fim dos voos diretos entre a capital acreana e Porto Velho deu-se cerca de dois meses após a empresa ter anunciado o retorno deste trecho , suspenso desde agosto de 2020. O g1 pesquisou nas três companhias que operam no estado e não localizou voos diretos para Rondônia.

A empresa ainda orientou que passageiros que compraram bilhetes diretamente com a Gol podem remarcar suas viagens, pedir crédito ou reembolso diretamente na Central de Atendimento 0300-115-2121. "Caso o pasageiro não aceite, pode deixar crédito na companhia ou pedir reembolso", disse Artur.

Já os clientes cujos bilhetes foram comprados com milhas podem fazer a gestão de suas reservas diretamente com a Smiles pelo telefone 11 991 824 233. Pasageiros que adquiriram bilhetes com agências devem procurar a própria a empresa que vendeu o passagem.

articles.title: Roberto De Zerbi's Spurs a complete team; Unai Emery works magic on Nicolas Jackson - Premier League hits and misses
articles.summary: Sky Sports' football writers analyse the Premier League action as Roberto De Zerbi gets Spurs ticking in statement win over Chelsea; Unai Emery works his magic on Nicolas Jackson again; Arsenal 'unlock' set-piece weapon; Gianluigi Donnarumma's aura of invincibility begins to fade
articles.body:
Was this the result when Roberto De Zerbi truly started to turn Tottenham's miserable decline around? Was this the performance when he discovered how to get the best out of his £185m midfield signings? Was this when his players' personality and motivation changed?

"Why not?" said De Zerbi after Tottenham's 2-0 win over Chelsea. It was a "different Tottenham", he said.

"Not a different attitude. Different relationships with the players, different group."

Tottenham have been threatening to improve. They should have won at Manchester United. They beat Coventry at home as expected. But this was a proper test albeit against a Chelsea side also finding their way under a new head coach. Spurs stood up to it.

"Before Man Utd, we spoke a lot in a big, big meeting, removing the mask and speaking honestly, clearly in front of ourselves," said De Zerbi. "And from that moment, I think we changed something in ourselves.

"We want to improve, improve, improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough."

From the moment Spurs changed ends at kick-off, a decision home fans groaned at, they had Chelsea where they wanted them despite the relentless wind and rain in their faces.

Omar Marmoush's first-half miss threatened the same old story, but perhaps their luck is changing now too. Mike Penders' error was a gift, but one that was deserved. Spurs will also argue a big decision went against them before the own goal, when Cole Palmer barged into Mateus Fernandes' head.

Fernandes also delivered the corner that Penders punched in. The midfielder was at the heart of everything. Playing at the base of Spurs' midfield three, he was outstanding. He had the most touches, passes, successful tackles and successful dribbles of any player on the pitch. His performance typified an evolving Tottenham side.

"We are working to change the last part of the club's history," said De Zerbi and they are heading in the right direction. David Richardson

Arsenal's perceived over reliance on set pieces was used as a stick to beat them with last season as they scored 25 goals from deadball scenarios, excluding penalties, en route to lifting the Premier League title.

It is an ominous sign for the rest of the league, then, that 'Set Piece FC' are level on points with leaders Manchester City having just scored their first set-piece goal, excluding penalties, in their eighth match.

Mikel Arteta warns that Ezri Konsa's goal from a corner in the 2-0 win over Everton will "unlock" Arsenal from set-pieces moving forward.

What chance do the rest of the league have if this Arsenal side, that have found ways to win without set-pieces, have rediscovered their not so secret weapon? Brace yourself, you're going to be seeing a lot more of set-piece coach Nicolas Jover on your TV screens. Zinny Boswell

Nicolas Jackson has always been a striker who gives you plenty to like and plenty to scream at. The running, the movement, the willingness to stretch defences and make life miserable for centre-backs have never really been in doubt. It is what happens when the ball reaches his feet in front of goal that has tended to leave manager's tearing their hair out.

But Unai Emery appears to be working his magic again.

Jackson's double in Aston Villa's 2-1 win over Manchester City took his tally to seven goals in eight starts for the club. It's not what we usually expect from Jackson.

Villa weren't buying a goalscorer. They have acquired a forward who brings so much to Emery's attacking structure. Jackson runs the channels relentlessly, occupies defenders and creates space for those arriving around him. Centre-backs do not get a quiet afternoon when he is leading the line. Man City, and especially Marc Guehi, found that out.

That industry has always been there. The difference now is the end product.

Villa have a striker who could take them to some special places this season. The hard yards were never the problem. Now the goals are following, too. Lewis Jones

There was a time when Gianluigi Donnarumma felt like a goalkeeper that was unbeatable. He was being talked about as one of the best in the world before he had even reached adulthood, making his Italy debut aged just 17 years and 189 days. That was 10 years ago.

His mistake in Aston Villa's 2-1 win over Manchester City was another reminder that there are cracks in the armour. Since the start of last season, no goalkeeper has made more errors leading to shots in the Premier League than Donnarumma, with seven. Three of those mistakes have resulted in goals.

That is a worrying trend for a goalkeeper operating at the very highest level. Errors happen, of course, but the frequency is becoming difficult to ignore.

There is an increasingly erratic element to his game with moments of uncertainty creeping into performances that once seemed defined by authority.

Perhaps the demands of English football are exposing weaknesses that were less obvious elsewhere. Perhaps it is simply a dip in form. Either way, City need their goalkeeper to be a source of security. Lewis Jones

Nottingham Forest are becoming the Premier League's most frustrating watch. Not because they are playing badly, but because they are doing almost everything right apart from the bit that matters most.

Their 1-1 draw at Ipswich was another case of dominance without the reward. Forest racked up 2.31 expected goals, won the shot count 17-7 and had enough opportunities to put this game to bed. Instead, Neco Williams' first-half strike was all they had to show for their superiority, allowing Ipswich to snatch a point.

This is becoming a worrying habit. No Premier League team has underperformed its expected goals tally more than Forest this season, scoring just six goals from chances worth 13.4 xG. That is a staggering shortfall and goes a long way towards explaining why they have managed just one win in eight games.

However, do not confuse poor finishing with poor football.

Forest rank sixth in the Premier League for expected goal difference, the measure of chances created minus those conceded. Opta's expected points model suggests they should have twice their current tally of six points. In other words, the underlying numbers paint the picture of a team performing considerably better than their results suggest.

Under an elite manager in Oliver Glasner, they are creating chances, controlling games and limiting opponents.

Forest are leaving points on the table. When their forwards finally start converting the opportunities their football deserves, they could be a very different proposition. Lewis Jones

articles.title: La Roma más argentina sobrevive a un espectacular derbi en Nápoles
articles.standfirst: Gol de Soulé y doblete del central Balerdi para igualar el 'show' de McTominay
articles.summary: Gol de Soulé y doblete del central Balerdi para igualar el 'show' de McTominay
articles.body: Fue un derbi a la altura de las expectativas. Nápoles y Roma empataron (3-3) en el Stadio Diego Armando Maradona en un duelo con cinco goles en la segunda parte y dos dobletes: el del escocés McTominay y el argentino Balerdi. 'La Loba' se queda tercera y podría alejarse del liderato... mientras que el Nápoles sigue lejos, en la décima plaza. El 'Derby del Sole' ponía a prueba a una Roma que seguía soñando a lo grande esta temporada. Gasperini, sin embargo, en el post de jornada Champions y antes de una fecha intersemanal de 'Calcio', metía cambios en el once mientras seguía sin recuperar a Koné, Dybala o Svilar. Y el Nápoles de Allegri, entre críticas, empezó mejor. La primera clara fue 'salvada' por Rensch bajo palos antes de que apareciera Lang para anotar el primero. Y aunque Malen avisó con un mano a mano errado ante Meret... fueron los del sur los que hicieron el primero. Lo logró Zambo Anguissa con una chilena preciosa e imposible para Gollini. La Roma se reactivó entonces y antes del descanso tuvo en la cabeza de Cristante la más cristalina: un cabezazo al palo a la salida de un córner. Pero el Nápoles hacía daño al contragolpe y Di Lorenzo perdonó lo que podría haber sido la sentencia. Gollini, sin embargo, se inventó una parada imposible para mantener a 'La Loba' en el partido. Todo pasó en un segundo tiempo estelar que fue el ejemplo de lo 'loca' que está siendo esta Serie A 2026-27. McTominay, que venía de ser clave en Champions, hacía el 2-0 a la salida de vestuarios. Pero Soulé no había tirado la toalla y lideró el intentó de remontada romano. Hizo el 1-2 y dio vida a una Roma que igualó el partido con un tanto de Balerdi a la salida de un saque de esquina. No acabó todo ahí. A McTominay le quedaba aun más por dar y el ex del Manchester United definió desde la frontal para devolver la locura al Stadio Diego Armando Maradona. Pero tenía tiempo la Roma para, de nuevo, agarrarse a los argentinos de su once. Balerdi cabeceó para el 3-3, doblete del central... reconvertido a '9'. Allegri, que acabó expulsado, ve como su Nápoles se aleja de las posiciones de cabeza mientras la Roma sobrevive a un 2-0 en contra y a otro visita complicada.

articles.title: Premier League Golden Glove live rankings: Updated goalkeeper standings for most clean sheets in 2026-27
articles.summary: While goals are the most exciting, and often most memorable, part of a team's charge towards the domestic league championship, defending is also a key part o...
articles.body:
The 2026-27 Premier League season promises to deliver thrills, excitement and memorable moments.

With Arsenal looking to defend their English top-flight title, the Gunners will look to get contributions from all over the pitch.

While goals are the most exciting and often most memorable part of a team's charge towards the domestic league championship, defending is also a key part of any team's trophy chase. Arsenal are a prime example of that, as goalkeeper David Raya has won at least a share of the Golden Glove award in each of the last few seasons.

The Sporting News looks at the 2026/27 chase for the Golden Glove award, given each year to the goalkeeper with the most clean sheets across the entirety of the domestic league campaign.

Premier League Golden Glove rankings 2026-27

Table updated after all games on Saturday, October 24.

Favorites, odds to win Premier League Golden Glove 2026-27

Last season's winner David Raya is the odds-on favorite to win the Golden Glove in the 2026-27 season, which is no surprise as Arsenal are considered one of the best defensive teams not just in England but across the whole of Europe.

Behind him are Man City's Gianluigi Donnarumma and Alisson Becker of Liverpool . Donnarumma finished second in last season's standings, but conceded three goals to Arsenal in the FA Community Shield to begin this new campaign, stoking fears of a regression. Alisson, meanwhile, struggled through injuries last campaign and thus was not near the top of the final list.

Who won Premier League Golden Glove 2025-26?

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya won the 2025/26 Premier League Golden Glove trophy, keeping a whopping 19 clean sheets across 37 games.

Premier League Golden Glove winners all-time

The Premier League Golden Glove award was first given out in 2005, when Chelsea legend Petr Cech set a Premier League record with 24 clean sheets, a mark that still stands today.

Cech also holds the record for most Golden Glove awards, level with Joe Hart , each winning four times.

articles.title: Why was Cole Palmer sent off against Tottenham?
articles.summary: Palmer was dismissed soon after Tottenham broke the deadlock through a Mike Penders own goal
articles.body:
Cole Palmer was sent off as Chelsea experienced a late capitulation to suffer their first home defeat to Tottenham since 2018.

The Blues fell behind in the 78th minute when 21-year-old goalkeeping understudy Mike Penders, making his full Premier League debut in the absence of the injured Emi Martinez, punched into his own net from a corner in the 78th minute.

Things then went from bad to worse for Xabi Alonso 's side in the pouring rain, with Blues talisman Palmer catching former team-mate and Chelsea youth product Conor Gallagher as he brought down a Spurs free-kick.

Palmer's studs caught the ankle of the midfielder, who had replaced James Maddison after he suffered another gut-wrenching injury setback in a Tottenham shirt.

Palmer and Chelsea players vigorously appealed for the decision to be overturned, which VAR does now have the power to do with second yellow cards.

But Chris Kavanagh stuck with his decision and Chelsea were reduced to 10 men.

Palmer will now miss Chelsea's trip to Liverpool for the Carabao Cup.

Palmer picked up his first yellow in similarly-dramatic circumstances, barging into a kneeled Mateus Fernandes with his torso after the Portuguese midfielder committed a cynical foul, pawing the bawl away while downed to stop Chelsea charging on goal.

A scuffle ensued which saw Fernandes and Micky van de Ven also booked.

Tottenham put the seal on a 2-0 victory seven minutes after Palmer's dismissal, with Mathys Tel finishing off a superb individual goal to wrap up Spurs' first triumph on Chelsea soil 2018.

articles.title: Malachi Toney Makes History as Heisman Buzz Stirs with Record-Setting Stats for Miami vs. Pitt
articles.summary: The connection between Miami stars Malachi Toney and Darian Mensah hit another high point on Saturday against Pitt.
articles.body:
The connection between Miami stars Malachi Toney and Darian Mensah hit another high point on Saturday against Pitt.

Toney gave his Heisman candidacy a big boost with a school-record 16 catches against the Panthers. He finished with 194 yards and three touchdowns.

Toney's first-half stat line with 12 receptions, 159 yards and two touchdowns is something that has only been done five times in the past 15 seasons by a Power 4 player.

This marks the second consecutive week and fourth time in seven games Toney has recorded at least 10 catches. It's his fifth time breaking the 100-yard mark.

Per FanDuel Sportsbook , Toney is third in Heisman odds at +500 (bet $100 to win $500). He is behind Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (+105) and Mensah (+300).

The Hurricanes teammates are in a difficult spot in that they can't differentiate themselves much in the Heisman race because of how much their mutual success is entwined.

Toney was a standout as a freshman in 2025 with Carson Beck as his quarterback, leading FBS with 109 receptions. This season has been a level-up moment. His two touchdowns in the first half against Pitt gave him 10 for the season, matching his 2025 total.

Mensah entered play on Saturday with 32 incompletions out of 167 attempts. He had 18 more completions to Toney entering the day than he did incomplete passes.

articles.title: Barnet: League Two side condemn racial abuse targeted at midfielder Isiah Noel-Williams
articles.summary: Barnet condemn racial abuse targeted at Isiah Noel-Williams after the midfielder was sent off in their 1-1 draw with Oldham.
articles.body:
Barnet have condemned racial abuse targeted at Isiah Noel-Williams after the midfielder was sent off in their 1-1 draw with Oldham.

Posting on X , external , the club shared a screengrab of a post on Noel-Williams' Instagram account, where a user had responded with a racist image.

"Barnet FC condemns in the strongest terms the racist abuse directed at Isiah Noel-Williams on Instagram following today's game," the club said in their statement.

"Isiah has our full and unwavering support. There is no place for racism in football, online or anywhere in society."

Noel-Williams signed for League Two Barnet from National League South side Hemel Hempstead Town in the summer.

The 23-year-old was sent off for a foul in the 70th minute at the Hive , with Oldham going on to score a 94th-minute equaliser.

articles.title: Pepelu lamenta cómo se le escapó el derbi al Valencia: “No se te puede ir un partido en el 93”
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista se refiere a la roja exprés a Harvey Elliott: "Lo expulsan, no sé por qué"
articles.summary: El centrocampista se refiere a la roja exprés a Harvey Elliott: "Lo expulsan, no sé por qué"
articles.body: El centrocampista del Valencia Pepelu, autor del gol valencianista de penalti y elegido MVP del encuentro, mostró su frustración tras la derrota por 1-2 ante el Villarreal en Mestalla, un partido que el conjunto de Javier Aguirre terminó perdiendo en el tiempo añadido pese a haber llegado por delante al descanso. Así se explicaba en Movistar tras el encuentro. ¿Ha sido una mala noche para el Valencia? "Sí, no ha sido un buen partido, sobre todo en la primera parte, pero hemos conseguido el premio de irnos por delante. No puede pasar más, nos expulsan a un jugador, no sé por qué, y no se te puede ir un partido en el 93". ¿Qué ha ocurrido en los últimos minutos? "Nada, la inercia de necesitar puntos, de ir hacia adelante, nos hemos quedado desprotegidos y nos han pillado la contra". ¿Ibais a por el partido? "Sí, al final, jugando en casa, necesidad de puntos, teníamos que ir a ganar. Pues desafortunadamente nos han metido a la contra, cosa que no nos puede pasar, así que nada, a seguir". Tres partidos después del cambio de entrenador, con dos empates y una derrota, ¿qué le falta al equipo? "Nada, seguir mejorando, seguir creciendo. Hemos estado cerca de las victorias en los tres partidos, al final son detalles que nos están penalizando y toca seguir".

articles.title: Aguirre sobre la expulsión de Elliott: "Absurda y ridícula, apenas habla español me irrita mucho"
articles.standfirst: El técnico dice que primero hablará con la plantilla: "Luego se los digo a ustedes"
articles.summary: El técnico dice que primero hablará con la plantilla: "Luego se los digo a ustedes"
articles.body: El entrenador del Valencia, Javier Aguirre, asumió toda la responsabilidad de la derrota por 1-2 ante el Villarreal en Mestalla y calificó el resultado como un golpe especialmente doloroso para su equipo, que sigue sin estrenarse con una victoria desde su llegada al banquillo valencianista. El conjunto blanquinegro se marchó al descanso con ventaja gracias al penalti transformado por Pepelu y llegó a los minutos finales con opciones de sumar los tres puntos, pero acabó cediendo tras encajar el tanto definitivo en el tiempo añadido. Después del encuentro, Aguirre evitó señalar a sus jugadores y se atribuyó los errores que acabaron condenando al equipo. “Distracciones, temas individuales, que la culpa es mía, evidentemente, porque yo elijo quién y cómo”, afirmó el técnico mexicano en unas escuetas declaraciones a Movistar, antes de reconocer que se trataba de una “derrota muy dolorosa”. Pese al desenlace, Aguirre defendió el trabajo realizado durante estas primeras semanas y mostró confianza en la evolución del equipo. “Hay que seguir, falta mucha Liga y estamos en la línea correcta, creo yo”, aseguró. Preguntado por los errores concretos que detectó en el partido y por las decisiones que pudo tomar de forma equivocada, el entrenador prefirió reservar cualquier análisis para el vestuario. “Primero le digo a ellos y luego a ustedes”, respondió. Aguirre también rehuyó valorar las acciones arbitrales que marcaron varios momentos del encuentro, entre ellas el penalti señalado a favor del Valencia y la expulsión sufrida por el conjunto local en la segunda mitad. “En 50 años desde que llegué al fútbol nunca he hablado de eso y hoy no será la excepción”, afirmó. Eso sí, valoró la expulsión de Elliott. "No estábamos mal en el tratamiento de la pelota y una expulsión absurda y ridícula de alguien que apenas habla español me irrita mucho. Y ya se lo dije a él. No es culpa de él, sino culpa mía totalmente por poner al que pongo. De puertas a dentro hablaremos". Cuestionado por el principal problema que atraviesa actualmente su equipo tras tres jornadas al frente del banquillo, el entrenador redujo la explicación a una cuestión de eficacia. “De resultados, resultados”, señaló. Con un balance de dos empates y una derrota en sus tres primeros encuentros, Aguirre insistió en la necesidad de seguir trabajando para encontrar cuanto antes el camino de la victoria.

articles.title: Irish Premiership: Brilliant Bannsiders return to summit
articles.summary: BBC Sport NI looks at title favourites Coleraine's fine start to the Irish Premiership season after the table-topping Bannsiders sweep aside 10-man Crusaders at Seaview.
articles.body:
It was Coleraine rather than Storm Boelo who wreaked havoc at Seaview on Saturday as they romped to a 5-0 victory over 10-man Crusaders.

Their biggest win of the season, and a fourth in a row since defeat by Linfield at the end of September, helped them leapfrog the Blues and return to the top of the Irish Premiership table.

It was a clinical and professional display from Ruaidhri Higgins' side in difficult conditions as they picked up a seventh away win from seven games on the road this season to open up a two-point gap at the summit.

There were four different scorers on Saturday (alongside an unfortunate own goal from Crusaders' Jacob Blaney) and all four were well-crafted.

After Scot Rough was sent off for a lunging challenge on Ben Wylie after 11 minutes, the midfielder produced a fine poked finish into the far corner for the opener seven minutes later.

Then, Senan Devine added a super second when he rifled into the top corner from range.

Captain Joel Cooper swept home a third to finish off a flowing team move before the break, with Blaney then turning home a corner for their fourth in the second half.

Former Crusaders striker Adam Brooks got off the mark for his new club as he slid in to score a fifth, again after some patient build-up play, to complete a satisfactory afternoon for the Bannsiders in north Belfast.

"It's a good day for us. We scored some brilliant goals. The first three goals are exceptional team goals," Higgins told BBC Sportsound.

"Don't get me wrong, the sending off definitely helped us, it was really early in the game.

"Seaview has been good to us in the last year, we have got good results here and scored lots of goals here and delighted with our afternoon's work."

Five-star Coleraine blow away 10-man Crusaders

Former Glentoran captain Paul Leeman, who was at the game as a co-commentator for BBC Sport NI, said that Higgins' side produced a "totally dominant display" in easing to victory.

"From the start of the game they came out with a real purpose, took the game to Crusaders early on and it looked like it would be difficult for Crusaders to contain them," he added.

"The second half they were professional. They controlled the game, managed the game and we saw some great goals. Coleraine really showed their quality."

Leeman singled out Wylie and Devine as standout performers, with both making meaningful contributions on a day in which the league's top scorer Matthew Shevlin struggled and missed a big chance to score.

With the game all but over as a contest after 40 minutes, the biggest challenge for Coleraine in the second half was the elements, which Higgins remarked were "as bad as you'll see".

"The rain and wind blowing a gale, it was difficult but I thought our players were really professional, applied themselves brilliantly and we got to use our squad today as well which was important."

A raft of second-half changes, including the introductions of the likes of Brooks, Lyndon Kane and Joe Thomson showed Coleraine's depth and helped them keep the intensity high against a young Crues side, with everyone desperate to stake a claim to play a greater role in upcoming big games against Glentoran and Linfield.

The stats make good reading for Higgins' men, who are living up to the billing as favourites to end a 52-year wait for the Gibson Cup this season.

The Irish Cup holders have only dropped five points from their 13 league games and last season's top scorers have already bagged 31 goals during this campaign while conceding just 12.

Taking on Glentoran in Duncan Ferguson's first game in charge on Friday followed by an away game against in-form Linfield on Saturday, 7 November in their next two games, both live on BBC iPlayer, will present much stiffer challenges for Higgins' side than they faced against the Crues.

Yet, they have already shown they can win in many different ways this campaign; whether it be ugly against the likes of Limavady, by coming from behind as they did against Larne, or in stylish fashion befitting of the quality they have in their squad, as they did on Saturday.

articles.title: El Villarreal sigue siendo el rey de los derbis valencianos
articles.standfirst: La victoria frente al Valencia prolongan el dominio amarillo que ya suma doce partidos consecutivos sin perder
articles.summary: La victoria frente al Valencia prolongan el dominio amarillo que ya suma doce partidos consecutivos sin perder
articles.body: El gol in extremis de George Mikautadze en Mestalla confirma que el Villarreal mantiene su corona como actual “rey” de los derbis valencianos. Y es que el conjunto amarillo sigue siendo el equipo más fiable de la Comunitat cuando toca medir fuerzas con sus vecinos. La victoria de este sábado ante el Valencia refuerza una tendencia que se prolonga ya desde hace varias temporadas. Además de la importancia de los puntos para un equipo que necesitaba un golpe de moral tras la derrota en Anfield, la realidad es que la rivalidad autonómica vuelve a teñirse de amarillo. En la presente temporada los de La Plana ya se han medido a los tres rivales autonómicos, con el balance de un empate ante el Elche (0-0) y dos victorias ante el Levante (3-1) y ahora el Valencia (1-2) Unos buenos números pero no tan espectaculares como los de la pasada campaña, donde el Villarreal firmó un pleno histórico al imponerse a sus tres rivales regionales en los partidos de ida y vuelta. En la primera vuelta derrotó al Valencia (0-2), al Elche (1-3) y al Levante (0-1). En la segunda, volvió a imponerse al conjunto valencianista (2-1) y al ilicitano (2-1), antes de cerrar la serie con una contundente goleada frente al Levante (5-1). Para encontrar la última derrota amarilla en un derbi valenciano hay que remontarse al 2 de enero de 2024, cuando el equipo cayó en Mestalla ante el Valencia (3-1). Desde entonces, el Villarreal acumula ya más de dos años y diez meses sin perder un partido de rivalidad autonómica, una secuencia que evidencia su regularidad frente a los representantes de la Comunitat. Y con cuatro equipos valencianos compartiendo categoría, la estadística adquiere todavía más relevancia.

articles.title: Íñigo: “La victoria es merecida, no por suerte”
articles.standfirst: El técnico amarillo destacó la estabilidad mostrada por su equipo en los peores momentos
articles.summary: El técnico amarillo destacó la estabilidad mostrada por su equipo en los peores momentos
articles.body: El técnico amarillo, Íñigo Pérez destaca el trabajo de su equipo y la capacidad de mantenerse estable pese a los momentos complicados que vivieron durante el partido. El navarro, como afirma cuando su equipo pierde, considera que la suerte no tuvo incidencia en el resultado final toda vez que destacó la figura de Alex Freeman. Su lectura “Creo que es una victoria merecida. Es cierto que se ha puesto complicada con su gol, tenía cierto miedo a que cayéramos en el descontrol. Llevo viendo varias semanas ya ante varios rivales que somos capaces de mantener el control. Lo vimos en Liverpool , donde nos mantuvimos estables con 4-2 y lo relaciono a lo que se ha visto hoy. Y eso se ha visto hoy. No nos hemos precipitado, hemos mantenido la pelota y esperar a que la gente que entra de fuera nos ayude. El Var: “Me mantengo al margen” No ganaron por suerte: “Por dejar clara mi opinión, no creo en la suerte en el fútbol y tampoco en que ya tocaba. Si no hemos ganado más ha sido por deméritos nuestros. Hoy hemos ganado y no ha sido por suerte, como cuando hemos perdido no ha sido por mala suerte. La capacidad de respuesta del equipo ha aumentado desde el inicio de temporada hasta ahora.Confían en el plan de juego, es importante mantener el equilibrio cuando no salen las cosas” Punto de inflexión: “Para bien o para mal, cuando pierdes hay que ser crítico y corregir. Cuando ganas todos están más contentos pero para lo que viene tiene poca influencia y para los próximos resultados. Sí que hace que tu forma de afrontarlo sea mejor, pero no nos pone en mejor disposición para ganar el martes en Manacor” Freeman por la izquierda: “El planteamiento inicial obedece a matices tácticos. Freeman tiene la capacidad de sostener a extremos como Otorbi, al que envía ánimos. Cardona venía con muchos minutos y creo que hay que gestionar esas cosas. Hay veces que sé que fallo en los cambios y debes purgarte, pero cuando parece que aciertas y el equipo gana tampoco me quedo con ello. Me quedo con cómo sonríen ahora en el vestuario” Sobreponerse a las adversidades: “Soy navarro, somos muy tercos. Y vengo de Vallecas donde peleábamos constantemente por todo. las dificultades son grandes pero no queda otra que insistir. Y por el entrenador no va a quedar” Sobre Freeman: “Los laterales del equipo son vitales para poder desarrollar como siento el fútbol. Los cuatro que tenemos son de muy alto nivel. Y son capaces de jugar en diferentes posiciones. Alex es un súper jugador. Puede jugará en muchos sitios, ese dinamismo y su nivel hace que yo sea más valiente con él. Es capaz de jugar con una tranquilidad pasmosa”

articles.title: Sam Parkin's EFL takeaways: Huddersfield on top, but Derby in the doldrums
articles.summary: BBC Final Score pundit Sam Parkin looks at the weekend's talking points in the EFL, including Huddersfield's fine form and QPR's big win over Swansea.
articles.body:
Final Score pundit and former Swindon, Luton and Northampton Town striker Sam Parkin selects his takeaways from the Championship, League One and League Two.

The Terriers are on a roll in League One, having won four of their last five under head coach Martin Drury and going unbeaten since losing to Bromley on 19 September. They beat Wigan Athletic 2-1 with Derensili Sanches Fernandes scoring once again.

Parkin: "I've been really impressed. Going back to last season, everyone had a lot of high hopes for them and it didn't materialise.

"It's been a terrific start and it's easy to look at some of the signings that have come in. It's more than just the two goal scorers today obviously, but Sanches Fernandes has been a revelation, he looks at the moment far too good for the level.

"You never know how it's going to go when a manager takes a team for the first time in the EFL, but I've heard a lot of good things about him as a coach and his his team look like they have all the credentials to get promoted this season."

On whether he thinks Sanches Fernandes is the best player in League One:

"I think so, yeah - he looks a class above. There were a couple of passes in recent games which really showed his quality, his awareness in the way to pass. He looks like a terrific player so whoever has done that bit of recruitment deserves a pat on the back."

The Robins are up to third after defeating in-form Newport County 1-0 at the EV Charger Points Stadium with a goal from Charlie McCann. Boss Steve Cotterill appears to have turned the fortunes of club around after returning for his second spell.

Parkin: "It's incredible really when you think about where (they were when) he took them on. When he took the job last season they were really adrift, so he's done a terrific job.

"It's obviously difficult at times, going back to somewhere where you're so fondly thought of, but you know he's replicating what what he did during his first bow and they absolutely love him there.

[Charlie] McCann is one of the stories of the season if you just look at his is goal record. All credit to him scoring goals and he was the difference maker again today.

"He missed a game through suspension recently and it affected them so he's become talismanic this season.

"Steve Cotterill has shown through the years that his teams are very difficult to play against but I've been equally as impressed with their work they are doing in possession, so they seem to have a really good thing going out down there at Cheltenham at the moment."

Derby County are currently 23rd in the Championship after drawing 1-1 with Sheffield United at Bramall Lane. John Eustace's men have not won a league match since 1 September.

Parkin: "They'll be bitterly disappointed with only leaving with a point although having said that, it looked like (goalkeeper Jacob Widell) Zetterstrom performed absolute heroics to maintain the point there at Bramall Lane.

"It was a really big game for both clubs today because they've had indifferent starts to the season.

"For Derby, they've had problems with injuries. Obviously there was there was hope of a takeover in the summer that hasn't materialised. They're working with a squad that maybe is not as strong in every department but hopefully the club can use that point as a positive in the in the next few weeks ahead.

"I've got confidence that John Eustace can turn it around."

Norwich City ended their five-game losing run in the Championship by coming from behind to win at Charlton Athletic and ease the pressure on head coach Philippe Clement.

Parkin: "They'll have to hope that this can be the turning point. What I will say in their favour is that they've got two very winnable games next if you look at where their opponents are positioned in the table, Watford and Derby.

"Defensively there's been enormous issues throughout the season and given that the personnel is quite similar to last season it's taking everyone by surprise.

"Obviously Mohamed Toure is missing. He probably has to be eased into the season given his injury issues and it didn't help losing [Ali] Ahmed just prior to the season to a serious knee injury. Kenny McLean's been missing as well so I think there are mitigating factors.

"You'd have to say that the manager [Clement], although he's got a lot of goodwill towards him in terms of the people at the club given how they performed last season, to ride out after straight defeats had they had they lost at the Valley would've been difficult. (It was) A much needed win against a Charlton side who've got big problems themselves."

Richard Kone scored a 15 minute hat-trick as QPR overwhelmed high-flying Swansea City 5-0 at MATRADE Loftus Road - his first goals since April. The Hoops now sit in eighth having only lost one of their last six matches.

Parkin: "I'm really pleased for Kone because he's a player that I really rate and I thought he was terrific during the early weeks of last season, especially when he was combining with [Rumarn] Burrell who unfortunately is out at the moment.

"For QPR those two looked like they had the makings of a really good partnership so yeah the loss of form has been a bit concerning from Kone because I thought that he had the potential to maybe become a Premier League player one day.

"It can still happen but he needs to find consistency in the Championship and yeah, this is an enormous confidence boost for him for the team.

"The manager [Julien Stephan} seemed a little bit downbeat this week but to recover from the Birmingham loss and win so emphatically against a side who've had such a terrific start of the season is a statement win for QPR.

"I've got no doubt that he is a really talented coach. I just wondered if this season was gonna be tail off now because of the injuries that he's had in his squad.

"But yeah, an incredible win for them and Kone could really could be a difference maker for QPR being in those play-offs at the end of season."

Sam Parkin was speaking to BBC Sport England's Ben Marvell.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin, LSU vs. Auburn Final Box Score, Top Player Stats and Highlights
articles.summary: Head coach Lane Kiffin led the No. 18 LSU Tigers to an impressive 38-17 SEC road win over the Auburn Tigers at Jordan-Hare Stadium in Auburn, Alabama, on Saturday.
articles.body:
Head coach Lane Kiffin led the No. 18 LSU Tigers to an impressive 38-17 SEC road win over the Auburn Tigers at Jordan-Hare Stadium in Auburn, Alabama, on Saturday.

Despite Auburn coming off an emotional upset win over then-No. 1 Georgia on the road last week, LSU was a 7.5-point road favorite on Saturday, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Quarterback Sam Leavitt did it all for LSU on Saturday in one of his best individual performances of the season.

Here's a look at how Leavitt and all of the key offensive contributors for both teams fared in the SEC clash:

After LSU and Auburn traded first-quarter field goals, LSU started to take the game over with back-to-back touchdowns.

The first was a 10-yard scoring strike from Leavitt to wide receiver Jackson Harris, and that was followed up with a 15-yard touchdown pass from Leavitt to tight end Trey'Dez Green:

On the heels of LSU going up by 14, Auburn answered on its ensuing drive when quarterback Byrum Brown scampered for a 34-yard gain down to the LSU 1-yard line before plowing his way into the end zone from one yard out on the next play:

That gave Auburn some much-needed momentum and got the crowd involved once again, but the good vibes were short-lived.

Just over a minute after Brown's touchdown, Leavitt hit Harris on a crossing route and Harris took it 70 yards for his second touchdown reception of the game:

Then, after an Auburn three-and-out on offense, LSU marched 74 yards on 10 plays, and Leavitt scored on a four-yard touchdown run with just 17 second left in the first half, extending the LSU lead to 31-10:

Following a scoreless third quarter, a 12-yard touchdown run by running back Dillin Jones early in the fourth quarter made the score 38-10 and essentially put the game out of reach:

LSU improved to 6-2 overall and 3-2 in the SEC with Saturday's win, keeping its College Football Playoff hopes alive in the process.

An eight-point loss to Ole Miss and a one-point loss to Kentucky represent the blemishes on LSU's record, but back-to-back wins over Mississippi State and Auburn have the Tigers back on track.

Following a bye next week, a gauntlet of a three-game stretch is on tap for LSU, as it will host No. 13 Alabama and No. 19 Texas before going on the road to face No. 11 Tennessee.

LSU may have to run the table in order to make the CFP, as there is no guarantee that Kiffin's squad will crack the top 11 of the CFP rankings with three losses.

Saturday's loss means Auburn is now 4-3 overall and 2-3 in the SEC, meaning head coach Alex Golesh still has work to do in terms of getting his team to bowl eligibility in his first season at the helm.

Given that games against Arkansas and Samford are still left on the schedule, Auburn seemingly has a solid chance to finish with a record of .500 or better for the first time since 2020.

Auburn has a tough matchup lined up for next Saturday, though, when it goes on the road to face No. 7 Ole Miss.

articles.title: Cardiff boss reveals Aberfan emotions after emotional tribute
articles.summary: Brian Barry-Murphy said it was imnportant his players understood what the day meant to supporters and all those impacted.
articles.body:
Cardiff City head coach Brian Barry-Murphy has spoken of the emotions surrounding tributes to the Aberfan disaster of 1966 that played a part in inspiring his side to victory over Birmingham.

Cardiff's squad and management had visited the memorial garden in the valleys village that, 60 years ago, saw 116 children and 28 adults die when a coal tip collapsed and engulfed Pantglas junior school.

Irishman Barry-Murphy said he had not fully appreciated the suffering and significance of the disaster in the area just 20 miles away from the Welsh capital.

And he had stressed to his players the importance of delivering a performance that "understood what we were playing for".

Salech ends Birmingham's unbeaten run on Cardiff return

The hero dinner lady who died saving five children in the Aberfan disaster

The portraits that helped bring the lost Aberfan children home

Latest Cardiff City news, analysis and fan views

"I had an awareness of what happened there, but I never knew the depth of what went on or what people experienced," Barry-Murphy said following the 1-0 victory.

"It was very important for the players to watch the footage to understand what the people there have been through.

"We organised to go there and it was very, very important.

"While you're there, it's naturally emotionally very difficult because you start to see the gravestones of the people who passed there.

"But also the stories of the different people there that day. It's very difficult to comprehend what they went through.

"Football is football and we couldn't guarantee that we were going to win today, but we had to produce a performance that looked as if we understood what we were playing for.

"On such a poignant day, it's very important that we played the way we did."

Barry-Murphy had written in the matchday programme - including a front cover displaying the clock found in the rubble that stopped at the time of the disaster - that the people of the community had shown what coming together means "in the most unimaginable of circumstances" and wanted his side to display the same qualities.

The game also saw a minute's silence held before kick-off, respected impeccably by Cardiff and Birmingham fans.

Barry-Murphy revealed that academy coach, Dennis Moss, also made the visit to Aberfan 24 hours before the 60th anniversary commemorations having been among the rescuers.

"He was one of the first responders as an 18-year-old from Cardiff who shot up there to start pulling bodies from the rubble," he said.

"He was there with us and you see the effect it had on him to be back there."

articles.title: Cincinnati ends No. 8 Texas Tech's undefeated season with 37-24 upset win
articles.summary: Cole Tabb's long TD run iced the game in the fourth quarter for the Bearcats.
articles.body:
No. 8 Texas Tech became the second undefeated team to go down in Week 8.

Just two days after James Madison's hopes of another unbeaten season ended , Tech lost 37-24 at Cincinnati. It's the first regular-season loss for the Red Raiders in over a year; Texas Tech last lost a regular-season game on Oct. 18, 2025, at Arizona State.

Cincinnati took a first-half lead and flipped the game in its favor late in the first half. After the Bearcats went up 17-6 with 1:37 to go, Texas Tech QB Will Hammond was intercepted by MJ Cannon with 37 seconds to go.

The Bearcats were seemingly content to take an 11-point lead into halftime. But Cole Tabb ripped off a 51-yard run on Cincinnati's first play and immediately put Cincy into field goal range. Four plays later, JC French IV threw his third TD of the first half when he found tight end Lyviel Waters with four seconds to go in the second quarter.

Another big run from Tabb put the game on ice in the second half. After Texas Tech cut Cincinnati's lead to 13 with a field goal, Tabb broke off a 58-yard TD run.

It's the Bearcats' first victory over a team in the top 10 of the AP Top 25 since the 2021 team that made the College Football Playoff and beat then-No. 9 Notre Dame to move to 4-0.

It was also a win that had Texas Tech Board of Regents chairman and Protect College Sports Act advocate Cody Campbell grousing on social media.

This Week 8 game was immediately one of the biggest in the Big 12 after QB Brendan Sorsby transferred from Cincinnati to Texas Tech following a breakout season in 2025. But Sorsby was a relative afterthought on Saturday after the revelations of his sports betting habits and his eventual departure from the Red Raiders long before the football season began.

Tech pushed to add Sorsby after the offense cratered in the College Football Playoff under previous quarterback Behren Morton. Hammond, who started that game against Arizona State, suffered a torn ACL while filling in for an injured Morton as the Red Raiders won the Big 12 a season ago.

But it's also fair to believe that a potential upgrade at quarterback wouldn't have been enough to hide the flaws on this Texas Tech roster. While Campbell may think there's no excuse or reason to lose a game like Tech did against the Bearcats, it's a loss that wasn't hard to see coming, either.

Last year's Red Raider team was powered by a defense that allowed fewer than 12 points per game. Linebacker Jacob Rodriguez was a turnover-causing machine and finished fifth in the Heisman Trophy voting. Edge rusher David Bailey's 14.5 sacks propelled him to the No. 2 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft and Romello Height added 10 sacks of his own. He's in the NFL too.

Though Texas Tech started the 2026 season 6-0 and was forcing turnovers at nearly an identical rate to 2025, there were clear signs that this team wasn't nearly as good as it was a year ago. Opponents averaged just 3.9 yards per play against Tech in 2025. Through seven weeks in 2026, they were averaging 5.1.

Even if the Red Raiders would have won on Saturday, they had plenty of competition at the top of the Big 12. No. 2 BYU looks better than it was a season ago, and No. 10 Utah also entered Week 8 undefeated. While Tech doesn't play either team from Utah in the regular season and the two rivals meet in November, there's no reason to think the Red Raiders are the favorites to go back-to-back.

articles.title: Rangers: Strikers finding form as Derek McInnes's side bounce back with 4-0 over St Johnstone
articles.summary: Derek McInnes demanded a response from his Rangers team after the disappointment of two dropped points at Dundee - and they delivered in emphatic style against St Johnstone.
articles.body:
Derek McInnes demanded a response from his Rangers team after the disappointment of two dropped points at Dundee last weekend - and they delivered in emphatic style to swot aside St Johnstone.

Other than a bit of a wobble at the start of the second half when Saints threatened to get back into the game, Rangers dominated and the 4-0 win in no way flattered them.

"Rangers were excellent for a number of reasons," former Rangers midfielder Andy Halliday said on BBC Radio Scotland's Sportsound.

"I thought it was as a positive 90 minutes as you can get. They created an abundance of chances. In the first half alone it should have been 4-0.

"It's always a positive when you come away with no injuries and your strikers are scoring goals again."

Podcast: Sportsound reaction to Saturday's fixtures

The goals and performances of Kevin Kelsy and Ryan Naderi at the top end of the pitch justified McInnes' decision to drop Djeidi Gassama to the bench and go with two strikers.

The two linked up well for Kelsy's opening goal and, with the Venezuelan coming away with a brace and Naderi a goal and an assist, the partnership provided more evidence they can spearhead Rangers' attack in the continued absence of Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti.

"Goals and assists for a striker make such a big difference in the style of play and how you approach the whole game," said ex-Rangers forward Peter Lovenkrands on Sportsound.

"You take shots, you are more confident with your touches, everything like that just gets better and better. This will do a world of good for Kelsy's confidence."

Rangers narrow gap on Celtic with thumping win over St Johnstone

Raskin happy at Rangers but unsure about January

The match stats tell the story of Rangers' dominance.

Their expected goals was 4.57 to St Johnstone's 0.58. They had 21 shots on goal, nine on target and created eight big chances to Saints' two.

They forced 13 corners and one of them led to a goal as Kelsy got on the end of Emmanuel Fernandez's flick-on to tuck home his second goal. It was the first goal Rangers have scored from a corner this season.

"One of Rangers' main strengths from last season was set-pieces," said Halliday.

"Rangers have had countless corners and wide free-kicks this season when it's not been James Tavernier delivering it. The standard of delivery this year has been really poor from set-pieces.

"They've got Naderi, Kelsy, Fernandez, they've got giants to hit but the delivery for the most part hasn't been good enough.

"On the 11th corner today they finally scored. Talk about adding strings to their bow. They need to get back to the point where they are a real danger from set-pieces."

McInnes felt the performance was "as good as we've been for a while" and it sets his team up nicely for Wednesday night's Scottish Premiership meeting with Hearts, the Rangers manager's first return to Tynecastle since swapping Gorgie for Govan in the summer.

"I had a brilliant time there and I know how difficult the fixture is for any opposition going to Tynecastle," said McInnes.

"We were unbeaten all season last season at Hearts and they've a strong home record, so we're going to have to bring a big performance to go there and get a result.

"We're well aware of that but I think we're in good form. We are slowly but surely just chalking off wins and there's loads of positives.

"It's never a bad thing when your strikers score and you go to any game, any venue, believing that you can get a result. We expect it to be tough but equally we want to make sure it's a tough night for them as well."

articles.title: Indiana survives against Michigan with 13-6 OT win in grueling defensive snoozefest
articles.summary: The Hoosiers were held scoreless in the second half by the Wolverines defense, but scored a touchdown in overtime to pull off the ugly win.
articles.body:
A week after its 22-game win streak was snapped , Indiana has bounced back with a 13-6 overtime victory over Michigan in the Big House and proved that ugly wins count all the same.

With Indiana held scoreless in the second half, Michigan had multiple promising drives that could have given them a lead. Instead, the Hoosiers' defense forced the Wolverines to settle for two field goals, including one in the final seconds of regulation. Michigan kicker Trey Butkowski, who had two field goal misses earlier in the matchup, was able to sink the 26-yard attempt to sent the game to overtime.

After showing off a deeply ineffective offense throughout regulation, Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover found the end zone shockingly fast once overtime began: Hoover's 21-yard pass to Brock Schott set the quarterback up to run in a touchdown on the next play.

That forced Michigan to score a touchdown to keep the game alive — something its offense had been unable to do all game. True freshman quarterback Tommy Carr, in his first start over the benched Bryce Underwood, ran for a crucial fourth-down conversion to keep the drive going, but he couldn't get a completion on the next set of downs.

The final incompletion was enough to secure the overtime win for the Hoosiers, who move to 7-1 on the season.

Mistake-riddled performances from Tommy Carr, Josh Hoover

Both defenses held strong to make the game a low-scoring slugfest, keeping it anyone's game until well into the fourth quarter. At one point in the final frame, the two defenses forced four consecutive three-and-out drives, making it feel like literally any completed pass could be a complete game-changer.

Both teams were forced into a number of offensive mistakes, with two interceptions, three missed field goals and 12 combined punts. Michigan recorded 224 total offensive yards; Indiana had 212. Both had third-down conversion rates around 30%.

Carr had a difficult game in his first start, losing a fumble, taking four sacks and throwing a tough interception. But even with the mistakes, the true freshman showed a little bit of promise, going 20-for-32 on passing for 167 and making some solid throws — though with no touchdowns.

Still, Carr and the Wolverines kept feeling like they were shooting themselves in the foot, especially with some of those promising chances in the second half. After coming out of halftime with renewed vigor, Carr strung together a 14-play drive that should have resulted in a touchdown, but Michigan couldn't push through the final yards, settling for a field goal — which Butkowski totally shanked with his second miss of the game. They had a second chance soon afterward, with Zeke Berry picking off Hoover on the next drive, and still couldn't find the end zone.

Hoover, meanwhile, had his worst game of the season and possibly his college career, going 8-of-18 on passing for 81 yards and throwing his first pick of the year to Berry. He did not complete a pass in the entire second half before overtime.

When speaking on the broadcast after the game, Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti admitted that Hoover "wasn't 100% today," but seemed satisfied with the win, ugly as it was.

"We found a way. Not pretty, but it's a win," Cignetti said. "It was gritty as hell. It's a win, and we're gonna celebrate it."

articles.body: Impensable a finales de agosto... pero real ahora. La Lazio de Gattuso duerme líder del 'Calcio' tras imponerse en el Olímpico de Roma al Parma con goles de Taylor y Diego Carlos, este en propia puerta. Los romanos, después de un verano convulso con protestas masivas de sus hinchas y ser eliminados en primera ronda de Coppa, son la gran sorpresa de esta temporada en Italia. Ante el Parma les costó imponerse... pero los goles llegaron en la segunda parte. El equipo de Gilardino, que no despega, solamente ofreció resistencia a través del portero Corvi pero cuando esta cedió, la Lazio fue capaz de dejar los tres puntos en casa. Kenneth Taylor, ex Ajax ahora despegando bajo las órdenes de Gattuso, hizo el primero. Y el segundo, el de la sentencia, fue en propia puerta del ex sevillista Diego Carlos. La reacción del Parma, ya tardía, llegó con el gol en el descuento de Lontani. La Lazio de Gattuso aventaja por ahora en tres puntos a un Inter que este domingo se enfrenta a la Fiorentina.

articles.title: Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta reveals he clips up Premier League managers stepping out of technical area
articles.summary: Arsenal comfortably beat Everton 2-0 at the Emirates Stadium to move level on points with Premier League leaders Man City; Mikel Arteta - shown a booking for stepping out of his technical area - believes other Premier League managers are getting away with committing the same infraction
articles.body:
Arteta joked about installing sensors on the sidelines, having been booked by referee Tony Harrington in the second half at the Emirates Stadium.

The Spaniard faces a one-match touchline ban if he receives another yellow card but believes other top-flight managers have repeatedly breached the rules without being punished.

"I do have to be careful, yeah," said Arteta. "I'm going to put sensors there!

"There are other managers (doing it), there are managers that have the record in the league: 36 times in 10 minutes they leave the touchline, no yellows.

"So I am clipping all of that so I have a massive storage of images, so if somebody comes to me (I can say) I'm not in the record yet, somebody else has the record."

Arsenal moved level on points with leaders Manchester City thanks to goals from centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel.

Konsa opened his account for the club in the seventh minute, converting from close range following a Martin Odegaard corner as the Gunners scored from a set piece for the first time this season.

Gabriel sealed victory with a 68th-minute header after recovering from an injury scare which left him down on the pitch requiring medical treatment.

Arteta believes the Brazil international's determination epitomises his team's character.

"The mentality of the team is the mentality of the individuals in the team," said Arteta.

"Gabi's a great example of that, because we were all scared, not because of the way he went down, but the reaction of the players that were next to him.

"Immediately he says he wants to continue and then he scores a goal to help us win the game. That's what we need from our players."

Arteta, who revealed substitute Riccardo Calafiori sustained a "slight" issue, also praised England international Konsa for adapting quickly following his summer move from Aston Villa.

"Unbelievable," said Arteta. "He's come to a huge club like Arsenal with no pre-season when (William) Saliba is here, with other players that are already here.

"And to position yourself in that manner, with that naturality and performing at the level that he's doing and building already a chemistry and a balance with Gabi that seems so solid, it's very, very difficult to do and we are really lucky to have him."

Everton manager David Moyes rued his side's slow start as they suffered a second successive defeat following last weekend's 2-0 loss to Chelsea.

Asked for his overall assessment, Moyes said: "Not an awful lot, really. I don't have big thoughts on it.

"I just felt we didn't really get to a level which I think would have been good enough to win on the day. We gave away a goal very early which meant we were chasing (the game).

"I felt we'd got a bit better in the second half, got a bit back into it a little bit more, got a bit closer to Arsenal and then they come up with the second goal.

"Some good stuff on the defensive side of it. I didn't feel we did enough on the attacking part of the game."

articles.title: El 'otro' Hazard impide que el París FC ponga la Ligue 1 del revés
articles.standfirst: Thorgan, hermano de Eden, entro desde el banquillo y, junto a Thauvin, lideró la remontada del Lens con un gol y una asistencia
articles.summary: Thorgan, hermano de Eden, entro desde el banquillo y, junto a Thauvin, lideró la remontada del Lens con un gol y una asistencia
articles.body: El curso pasado, el París FC volvió a la Ligue 1 cerca de medio siglo después. Salvaron la categoría con holgura y, habiendo invertido casi 80 millones en materia de fichajes, tenían en su mano dormir en lo más alto de la tabla. Ahora bien, el Lens —mejor local de la temporada pasada— siempre vende cara su piel en el Bollaert-Delelis... y acabaron remontando (2-1) con la colaboración de un Thorgan Hazard que marcó un gol y repartió una asistencia entrando desde el banquillo. La dirección del encuentro durante toda la primera parte apuntó sobre la portería del París FC. Sobre todo, desde la habitual insistencia del Lens a la hora de meter balones tensos desde los costados. Así llegó el penalti por mano de Coppola corregido por el VAR y el 'cabezazo' de Sotoca que se marchó rozando la madera. Thauvin, a escasos minutos antes del descanso, buscó resolver un centro de Abdulhaim con un 'taconazo'. No llegó a conectar con el balón y, en una de sus primeras salidas, el París FC tejió una contra que dejó helado el Stade Bollaert-Delelis. Combinaron Coppola, Pagis y Sinayoko para que Koleosho batiese a Risser con un disparo raso ajustado al palo. El 0-1 encajado en el descuento de la primera parte supuso un duro golpe para un Lens que, nada más volver de vestuarios, pudo quedarse con uno menos. Sinayoko peinó un balón a la altura del medio campo y, cuando Kebbal ya había arrancado, Todibo le agarró. El VAR, sin embargo, entró para intervenir... entendiendo que Baidoo podía llegar a la cobertura. Superado el susto, el propio Kebbal no pudo resolver peor otra contra que debió haber duplicado la ventaja para el París FC. Reaccionó Cahuzac dando entrada a Kyllian Antonio y a un Thorgan Hazard cuyo impacto fue inmediato. Combinó con Thauvin y esté 'clavó' un remate al palo corto tras 'surfear' por la frontal para firmar el 1-1 en el 63'. El empate le valía al París FC para amarrar el liderato. Sin embargo, el hermano menor de Eden tenía ganas de fiesta y, a poco más de cinco minutos para el final, Thauvin le devolvió el favor para que anotase su primer gol en Ligue 1. El atacante galo, que cuajó otro recital, le puso un centro desde el costado izquierdo que mandó a guardar desde dentro dentro del área para certificar la remontada del Lens.

articles.title: Ni Julián pensaba revertir su situación tan pronto...
articles.summary: La contra crónica del Atlético-Deportivo
articles.body: Dos goles le han bastado a Julián para recibir el perdón. Al menos, de la mayor parte del Metropolitano. Salvo el fondo, que le recibió de nuevo con música de viento, el resto del estadio coreó a la Araña con el 1-0. Al grito de Julián del speaker... llegó el "Alvarez" de un amplio sector de los casi 70.000 aficionados que casi llenan el estadio. La realidad, que pocos esperaban (dentro del club) que el argentino diera la vuelta a su situación. Al menos tan pronto. Dos gples le han bastado. Pasó en Stuttgart, donde Marc Pubill falló (entre otras) la jugada que acabó con el gol local. Ante el Deportivo, como en otros encuentros de la temporada, se vio a un central irreconocible comparado con el del curso pasado, cuando llegó como lateral y Simeone le convirtió en uno de los mejores centrales de LaLiga. De momento, poco queda de la versión top del ex del Almería. Pronto, así confían en la caseta, llegara el que asombró hace justo un año. Vulgar. Así puede definirse la primera parte del Atlético ante el Deportivo, que manejó mejor el esférico y quiso hacer más que un equipo, el rojiblanco, con pocas ideas y cero intensidad. Apenas dos chispazos de Kang in, apenas dos momentos de inspiración, hicieron peligrar a la meta visitante. Ante el Stuttgart ya pasó que los del Metropolitano no saltaron al verde con la actitud adecuada. Como en Alemania, por cierto, la Cholina funcionó en el descanso y el equipo resurgió. No había pasado apenas nada en la primera media hora de un Atlético-Deportivo más que insulso hasta que un balón lateral sacado por un Yeramay, que minutos después dejó retratado a Barrios con una genialidad, la puso en el área. Dudó Oblak en la primera, pero no así sacando un gol claro a un Amatucci que es la última víctima del esloveno. Una más. "Respeto al que siempre nos respetó. Giménez uno di noi". Así rezaba la pancarta del fondo sur del Metropolitano para recibir a uno de los suyos. Sin duda, Josema es uno de los futbolistas que más calado en una hinchada que valora los que no regatean esfuerzos. De ahí los cánticos y la ovación cerrada de la afición para recordar a Giménez que siempre será un rojiblanco más.

articles.title: El Oviedo, con dos goles en dos minutos, amarga el récord al Almería
articles.standfirst: Si en la primera parte Arribas y Miguel marcaron, en la segunda Jacobo y un autogol de Pulido neutralizaron el marcador
articles.summary: Si en la primera parte Arribas y Miguel marcaron, en la segunda Jacobo y un autogol de Pulido neutralizaron el marcador
articles.body: El Almería dejó escapar una victoria que parecía tener en el bolsillo y vio cómo se esfumaba, en apenas dos minutos, un récord histórico de ocho triunfos consecutivos. Los rojiblancos dominaron durante gran parte del encuentro y se adelantaron con los tantos de Sergio Arribas y Miguel de la Fuente en la primera mitad, pero el Oviedo mejoró en la segunda e igualó en el tramo final con un golazo de Jacobo González y un tanto en propia puerta de Pulido tras otro centro del extremo madrileño para firmar un 2-2 que dejó helado al UD Almería Stadium. Almería y Oviedo comenzaron el encuentro con dificultades para hacerse con el control del juego. El balón parado rompió el ritmo frío de los primeros compases y permitió a los rojiblancos abrir el marcador. En un saque de esquina botado en corto, Quim puso un magnífico centro al segundo palo que Arribas remató de primeras con la izquierda para firmar el 1-0. El Oviedo reaccionó apenas cuatro minutos después con un disparo al larguero de Enzo Pérez tras una gran acción individual cerca de la línea de fondo. Sin embargo, el Almería de García Pimienta no suele perdonar. Miguel de la Fuente recibió dentro del área, se giró con un gran reverso y batió con un disparo seco a Aarón ante la pasividad de una zaga oviedista incapaz de evitar el 2-0. Quim estuvo cerca de sentenciar el choque con el tercer tanto, pero Aarón respondió con una buena intervención abajo para desviar su remate. Pese al marcador, el conjunto de Calero no bajó los brazos y siguió generando peligro con dos disparos lejanos de Goti y Enzo Pérez, bien resueltos por Andrés Fernández. Antes del descanso, Dani Calvo también rozó el gol con un cabezazo a la salida de un córner que se marchó por muy poco junto a la portería local. La segunda mitad comenzó con varios minutos de retraso debido a problemas de comunicación entre el árbitro principal y la sala VOR de Las Rozas, incidencias que se prolongaron durante buena parte del encuentro. Calero agitó el banquillo tras el descanso y el Oviedo dio un paso al frente. Estanis estuvo cerca del 2-1 en dos ocasiones, pero ambos remates se marcharon por muy poco. El partido cambió por completo con la entrada de Jacobo González. En su primera intervención, el madrileño firmó un auténtico golazo con una volea desde la frontal para recortar distancias en el minuto 88. Apenas dos minutos después volvió a ser decisivo al provocar el empate con un centro que Pulido desvió a su propia portería en el 90'. El Almería dejó escapar una oportunidad de oro para ampliar su ventaja al frente de la clasificación y vio cómo el Oviedo, con una espectacular reacción en el tramo final, frustraba el récord histórico de ocho victorias consecutivas de los rojiblancos con el definitivo 2-2.

articles.title: Uno a uno: Oblak camina silenciosamente hacia su séptimo Zamora
articles.standfirst: Como si no fuera con él, Jan salva sobre la línea un remate a quemarropa de Kevin en la última jugada del partido para asegurar otro triunfo del Atlético
articles.summary: Como si no fuera con él, Jan salva sobre la línea un remate a quemarropa de Kevin en la última jugada del partido para asegurar otro triunfo del Atlético
articles.body: El Atlético encadenó su sexto triunfo consecutivo con menos brillo de lo habitual pero con un Oblak tan extraterrestre como toda su vida. Siempre está, da igual cuando se lea. Se hizo gigante ante Amatucci en el 27' para evitar que empujara el balón que había dejado suelto tras una falta botada por Yeremay. También atajó sin problemas un disparo de Nsongo en la segunda mitad. Pero como si no fuera con él, aún salvó sobre la línea un último disparo de Kevin en la última jugada del partido. Camina silenciosamente hacia su ¡séptimo¡ Zamora. NOTA: 9 Más errático y menos seguro de lo habitual en la primera parte actuando como lateral, mejoró en la segunda, cuando puso su vigor y despliegue al servicio del equipo como doble pivote. NOTA: 5 Completamente desconocido, una mala sombra de lo que fue la temporada pasada. Inseguro con el balón, flojo en los duelos y con despistes 'imperdonables' como el que le costó el gol en Stuttgart en la primera parte que completó como central. En la segunda pasó al lateral y aunque se entonó como lateral, necesita volver por sus fueros. NOTA: 4 Fue el más firme de la zaga, consistente en la defensa del área y sin pérdidas en el inicio del juego en los primeros 45 minutos. La única mala entrega propició una buena ocasión para Nsongo, pero en general despachó una actuación aseada. NOTA: 6 Empezó intentando sorprender atacando por el carril central, pero su animosidad inicial fue decayendo poco a poco. Eso sí, tras el descanso recuperó la energía para culminar una buena acción colectiva con un pase de la muerte medido para que Julián hiciera el 1-0. NOTA: 6 Le costó entrar en acción en su regreso a la banda, pero en un minuto demostró su talento: primero, con una jugada individual, regate a regate, que acabó con un lanzamiento que rozó los palos; después con un golpeo marca de la casa desde fuera del área que se le fue alto por poco. Además, no tuvo problema para defender como quinto hombre cuando fue necesario. En la segunda parte, de nuevo libre por el centro, empezó muy asociativo, pero, ya desfondado, fue relevado en el 62'. NOTA: 6 Por momentos fue el acompañante más cercano de Julián en el afán por aprovechar su llegada y lectura del juego. Como casi siempre, también fue el más clarividente en la construcción. Y como tampoco ahorra ni el más mínimo esfuerzo y lo juega todo, fue sustituido al descanso para que pueda seguir siendo decisivo toda la temporada. NOTA FINAL: 6 Bien situado, pero bastante intrascendente, especialmente en ataque. Tampoco fue ninguna escoba en la recuperación. Al fichaje más caro de este verano se le debe presuponer mucho más. NOTA: 4 Otro de los que está alejado de su versión del curso pasado. Ha perdido el desborde y la verticalidad, incluso parece que se atreve menos a intentarlo. Tampoco explota su velocidad al espacio. NOTA: 4 También le costó rendir al estelar momento con el que ha empezado el curso antes del descanso. De hecho, tras el paso por los vestuarios fue clave para dibujar la jugada con la que Julián abrió la lata. Su apertura a Grimaldo dio fe de su facilidad para ver el fútbol. NOTA: 6 Se le vio con ganas de redimirse, especialmente con esforzadas carreras hacia atrás para ayudar en la recuperación, desde el principio. No obstante, no sería hasta que apareció donde debía para empujar el gran servicio de Grimaldo cuando acabó de ganarse el perdón de la mayoría del Metropolitano. Sin duda, era el gol que necesitaba. NOTA: 7 Más contenido que en sus últimas apariciones, sin excesivos problemas para defender. NOTA: 5 A falta de brillo en la mayoría de sus compañeros, su intensidad y su energía fue oro para revitalizar e imprimir energía al equipo. NOTA: 6 Peleó con los defensas y mostró sus ganas de empezar a ser importante tras un verano muy difícil. NOTA: 5 Entró en el tramo final, en un momento complicado en el que el Deportivo se vino arriba y se implicó especialmente en defensa para abortar un ataque peligroso. NOTA: 5 Tras una primera parte gris, apretó las tuercas al descanso y la reacción no se hizo esperar. Después, pese a seguir moviendo las piezas para que no decayera el equipo, no pudo evitar el sufrimiento final. NOTA: 6

articles.title: Giménez: "Yo soy un peón más de la gente que maneja este circo... mi fin es trabajar"
articles.standfirst: El central del Deportivo analizó su regreso al Metropolitano.
articles.summary: El central del Deportivo analizó su regreso al Metropolitano.
articles.body: José María Giménez atendió a los medios tras el final del partido en el que regresaba al Metropolitano. El partido: "No sumar no sirve de nada. El equipo hizo un gran trabajo ante un gran rival. Merecimos el empate, no se pudo. A seguir, a pensar en Copa y después el partido de Liga que hay que ganar". Clave: "Detalles puntuales que te condenan. Es evidente que hay mucha jerarquía arriba en el Atlético. Ese gol nos penalizó. No bajamos los brazos. Merecimos el empate". Recibimiento: "Esto es fútbol. Yo soy un peón más de la gente que maneja este circo. Mi fin es trabajar. Agradecido a todo el amor y cariño que me brindó el Metropolitano. De corazón, muchas gracias. Los voy a llevar siempre conmigo". Su partido: "Traté de no centrarme en lo emocional. Vine a hacer lo mejor posible para ayudar al equipo y tratar de sacar un punto que no se pudo dar".
