articles.title: Julián... y perdón por el fútbol
articles.standfirst: El primer gol del argentino en el Metropolitano esta temporada soluciona un partido infame del Atlético ante un Deportivo inocente, que lamenta la que marra Kevin en la última jugada
articles.summary: El primer gol del argentino en el Metropolitano esta temporada soluciona un partido infame del Atlético ante un Deportivo inocente, que lamenta la que marra Kevin en la última jugada
articles.body: "¡Julián!”, repetía el de megafonía. “¡Álvarez!”, coreaba buena parte de la grada. Y así, unas cuantas veces. Si no fue el quite del perdón, al menos lo pareció. Vuelven las aguas a su cauce con el argentino, o esa pinta tiene por la reacción mayoritaria, más allá de que su gol se tradujera en tres puntos para un Atlético que en todo caso tiene que hacérselo mirar. Porque, puestos a reclamar disculpas, como se le ha reclamado al chico no sin razón, muchos de los que se ponen la rojiblanca deberían excusarse por un partido infame con un final que ni siquiera fue feliz sino agónico. Con toda la portería para él, Kevin envió a Oblak el último toque del partido. El que hubiera valido el empate. El Deportivo nunca terminó de creerse que aquello de enfrente era un guiñapo. Apenas dos ocasiones recolectó la escuadra herculina en un primer acto bochornoso del equipo de Simeone, la falta de Yeremay que Oblak despejó de aquella manera, concediendo una segunda opción para Amatucci a la que también se opuso el esloveno, y el cabezazo de Villares a servicio desde la izquierda de Quagliata. Por lo demás vivió la mar de tranquilo el conjunto blanquiazul, firme atrás, aseado con la pelota y, posiblemente, sorprendido con lo que temía batalla y no llegaba a escaramuza. No había por dónde coger a ese Atlético de los primeros 46 minutos. Llorente y Pubill han hecho suya la teoría del ínclito De Paul (ésa de que después de ser campeón del mundo “ya no hay más nada”), Hjulmand no aportaba, Barrios parecía jugar con miedo a la lesión, Lookman y Julián se sostenían en su línea mediocre habitual... Ni siquiera con Baena podía contarse esta vez, así que incluso un estadio más bien paciente como el Metropolitano tiraba de música de viento sobre la media hora. Es posible competir, espetaba El Cholo en la previa. Pero así no, desde luego... El caño que tiró Yeremay a Barrios sirve como perfecta metáfora del intervalo en cuestión, aunque Julián, Barrios, Kang-in o Hjulmand fueran probando suerte con disparos que no movieron una ceja del personal. Más allá de los lesionados, el único tipo al que Simeone (Diego Pablo) había dejado en el banquillo por aquello de las rotaciones era Simeone (Giuliano), cuestión a la que conviene atender por aquello de que el chico, con todas las limitaciones que se le busquen y encuentren, rebosa al menos el orgullo del que parecían carecer los que sí estaban sobre el terreno de juego. Al menos buena parte de ellos. Hubo que tirar de él, claro. Y de Le Normand, de paso, moviendo de sitio a unos cuantos. Quizás por el qué dirán, el Atlético dibujó una jugada potable en la reanudación, con Baena abriendo, Grimaldo poniéndola y Julián embocando para que tomara forma el primer párrafo de esta crónica. Por fin con ventaja, las tuvo el cuadro local a la contra, las cosas como son, una de Julián, otra de Sorloth, una más de Giuliano, aunque el fútbol seguía siendo pobre. Por entonces tampoco es que el Deportivo terminara de reaccionar, por muchos cambios que hiciera Hidalgo. Y a todo esto, Giménez. El uruguayo no se habría planteado un retorno tan cómodo como el que tuvo, ni dos meses han pasado desde que se certificó una salida que se podía entender acaso desde el fondo, en ningún caso desde las formas. De hecho se fue para que pudiera venir uno que al final no vino, así funciona esta Dirección Deportiva a la que por lo visto hay que dar la razón sí o sí. El caso es que con ventaja mínima local todos los ojos apuntaban a Josema en las que a última hora puso su equipo en el área. Pero en realidad las tuvo Kevin. Ésa y otra antes. Fue que no, así que valió la de Julián. En cuanto al fútbol, mil perdones.

articles.title: Chelsea: Cole Palmer red card, Mike Penders howler and 'out-coached' by Roberto De Zerbi on horror night for Xabi Alonso
articles.summary: Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for just the second time in 35 visits in the Premier League; Chelsea created very little in the defeat with Gary Neville calling them 'awful'; Cole Palmer was described as 'petulant' following his red card; Mike Penders made a 'monumental' error
articles.body:
Spurs had won only one of their previous 34 Premier League visits to Chelsea but dominated Xabi Alonso's side from start to finish, with an own goal from Mike Penders and a stunning late strike from Mathys Tel securing a well-deserved win for Roberto De Zerbi's side.

To add to their woes, on an evening where the dismal weather matched their performance, Cole Palmer was sent off for a second bookable offence after already escaping a straight red card earlier in the game, having barged into Spurs midfielder Mateus Fernandes.

"Tottenham outplayed Chelsea. Out-coached, everything. None of us expected Tottenham to come here and win today, but after 10-15 mins, that confidence did start to grow," said Neville while on commentary, in a game that was also described as the worst performance of Alonso's short tenure so far.

"Chelsea have been awful, really. On the ball, they've been well short. Nowhere near the level. I am stunned."

Chelsea started without a recognised striker after Joao Pedro was unexpectedly absent.

Both Danny Welbeck, who started as the striker in the 3-0 loss to Brentford when Joao Pedro was also out injured, and Estevao were on the bench. Chelsea didn't bring on Welbeck until the 88th minute when they were 2-0 down.

Neville added: "Welbeck must be thinking, 'How do I get a game here?' Disciplinary problems have cost him [Alonso] today, but I don't think that's the biggest problem.

"The biggest problem is that Tottenham have come and outplayed them. They've made them look really ordinary.

"Where Tottenham have absolutely battered Chelsea is in midfield. Cole Palmer, [Morgan] Rogers, [Jordan] Henderson and [Moises] Caicedo have been able to get nowhere near. Spurs' midfield has run the game.

"They absolutely bossed the game. I usually say when it's bad weather and teams are getting pressed, knock it long. I think it's mad.

"But you could just see that Chelsea wouldn't be able to keep that pressure on. Tottenham's combinations and patterns in midfield were really good."

'Petulant' Palmer and Chelsea's frustration

Chelsea's frustrations, and Palmer's in particular, were clear throughout. After Fernandes deliberately handballing to stop him on the counter, Palmer confronted the Spurs midfielder after the whistle.

The England international barged into Fernandes, sparking a melee between the two sides. Sky Sports News understands the incident was checked and cleared by VAR John Brooks.

"I think that could be a red. If this wasn't at Stamford Bridge, I think it's a red," Neville said at the time of the incident, which ended in only a yellow for Palmer.

Jamie Redknapp said the reaction was "petulant" and out of character for a player who is usually known for his cool and composed nature.

Just three minutes after Penders' own goal, the forward then caught Conor Gallagher late and was swiftly shown a second yellow by referee Chris Kavanagh.

"They started to lose their heads. It was frustration as they couldn't get near them," Redknapp continued. And that spread across the team as a whole, not just with their talisman Palmer.

Morgan Rogers was also booked after catching Gallagher, the same player who was the target of Palmer's second tackle, in an incident Neville believed could have reduced Chelsea to nine men.

"I think that's a red. I do," Neville added. "He's absolutely wellied him with no intent. That's ludicrous from Rogers. They have lost it. Xabi Alonso needs to get them off."

'Monumental' error from Penders - but he's their only option

Penders' howler, punching the ball into his own net from a corner, came in his first start, replacing the injured Emiliano Martinez.

After falling behind 1-0, Chelsea unravelled. But with Martinez set to be sidelined for the foreseeable future after facial surgery following a jaw fracture against Everton, the goalkeeper will need to bounce back quickly ahead of facing Liverpool in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, live on Sky Sports.

"He made a monumental mistake; it's as simple as that. The ball comes in and where he goes wrong is that he comes with no authority," Redknapp said.

"He, to a certain extent, gets bullied. There is hesitation. It's hard. It has to become character building for him. He has to fight within himself.

"They will need to put their arm round him; he is going to play again next week.

"Of course you will make mistakes but it is how you handle it. He has to get on with it and show some character."

Chelsea sanctioned Robert Sanchez's loan move to Como after Martinez arrived from Aston Villa in the summer.

Their other option in goal against Spurs was 23-year-old Teddy Sharman-Lowe, who spent last season on loan at Bolton and has not made a competitive senior appearance for the Blues.

Gabriel Slonina remains at the club but has not been named in the squad since pre-season.

The stats behind Chelsea's horror-show vs Spurs

Spurs gained just their second away win in 35 attempts against Chelsea in the Premier League (D11 L22) and their first since April 2018 (3-1).

Spurs have beaten Chelsea in all competitions at Stamford Bridge while keeping a clean sheet for the first time since December 1986 (also 2-0).

Chelsea failed to score at home in a Premier League London derby for just the second time in their last 17 such games, after a 0-0 draw with Crystal Palace on MD1 last season.

Chelsea's Mike Penders (21yrs 85d) is the second-youngest goalkeeper to score an own goal in the Premier League, after Illan Meslier (20yrs 354d) for Leeds against Wolves in February 2021.

Chelsea have conceded eight goals from set pieces in the Premier League this season, double the amount of any other side.

Cole Palmer's sending-off was the 100th red card Chelsea have been shown in the Premier League (excluding rescinded cards), becoming the third team to reach this milestone after Everton (113) and Arsenal (110).

Mike Penders became just the second Chelsea goalkeeper to score an own goal in a Premier League match, after Petr Cech against Everton in December 2009.

Chelsea had just seven attempts against Spurs, their fewest in a Premier League game this season and their fewest at home in the competition since January against Brentford (6).

articles.title: Tottenham Hotspur: Are Roberto de Zerbi's side finally on their way back after win at Chelsea?
articles.summary: Tottenham end Saturday's Premier League action in 12th place, their highest league position since 2 January. Are they finally on their way back?
articles.body:
Whisper it quietly, but could Spurs finally be on their way back?

Tottenham's 2-0 win at Chelsea on Saturday moved them up to the heady heights of 12th in the Premier League - their highest league position since 2 January.

And, after back-to-back 17th-placed finishes, there are growing signs Roberto de Zerbi's side are showing there is real light at the end of a pretty dark tunnel.

Saturday's impressive win at Stamford Bridge was just the second time they have won two league games in a row in 42 attempts - inspired by starring roles from James Maddison and Mathys Tel.

It was also the first time they have enjoyed as much as 68% possession in a match since April 2025.

The win was deserved too, although Chelsea certainly gave them a helping hand with goalkeeper Mike Penders punching the opener into his own net and Cole Palmer sent off for two yellow cards.

Spurs had taken seven attempts to get their first league win of the season against Coventry on Monday and on Saturday they looked transformed from the side that did not even score a goal until September 1.

It left De Zerbi glowing with positivity, despite another injury setback for Maddison, as he highlighted a team meeting earlier this month that sparked their revival in fortunes.

"Seven points after Manchester. Before Manchester we spoke a lot, we had a big meeting," he said. "We removed the masks and spoke honestly and clearly in front of ourselves. From that moment, I think something started to change within us.

"I think we have put something different into Tottenham in the last period. Not a different attitude, but different relationships with the players, different relationships within the group.

"We have changed the spirit of the group and improved the performances of the players, especially some of the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We have suffered enough."

Former Chelsea goalkeeper Rob Green added on BBC Radio 5 Live: "A dream afternoon for Tottenham . They looked controlled, looked at ease, they looked like they were comfortable on the ball.

"Results like this galvanise a side. When you look at the players coming back, yes Maddison got injured and he'll be a question mark over the next few weeks, but players coming back, momentum coming back - you feel, and say it quietly, Tottenham might just be coming back."

'A big statement' as Maddison and Tel star

Italian De Zerbi was appointed Spurs boss at the end of March 2026 with the club in crisis.

He arrived as the club's third manager of the campaign and, with seven games remaining, Tottenham were just one point clear of the drop zone.

After securing safety, albeit after a few scares, the club spent more than £300m on summer signings for the first time in their history as they backed De Zerbi to restore them to former glories.

And, after a slow start to the campaign and still lacking firepower in attack, the long-suffering Tottenham fans will be left feeling more positive than they have done for a long time.

" Tottenham have made a big statement in a really convincing performance," former Arsenal defender Martin Keown told BBC Sport.

"I thought Maddison was magnificent in midfield. He's like the Artful Dodger, isn't he? That midfield is full of mischief, but he's brave against the ball.

"I thought Tel was magnificent out on the left-hand side, [Mohammed] Kudus on the right was also really effective, and everybody really managed to handle the ball really well on the night.

" Spurs had almost 70% possession, which is remarkable for a team which was just a few places from the bottom of the table. I think what's changed for Spurs is the key personnel."

De Zerbi ran on to the pitch to celebrate with the travelling supporters at the final whistle, while his coaches and substitutes raced towards the players in the corner of the ground.

He has previously spoken of how he inherited players that cried after matches and lost all confidence - and believed his unprecedented control over the summer transfers was vindication for Spurs from last season.

It was fitting that Tel, who has attracted criticism from his own supporters since arriving from Bayern Munich for £30m in June 2025, provided the decisive moment to seal just a second league success in 36 years at Chelsea - a stunning low finish after a driving run.

The French forward, 21, told Sky Sports: "It is very special because we have come to Chelsea so many times and not got a win. We showed great mentality today and we need to enjoy this win.

"We created a lot of chances today. We walk out together, the goal is something special for me, I'm happy about it and let's keep pushing now."

Summer signing Matheus Fernandes added: "We are here to change the club's mentality, we want to beat the top teams, and make this victory for the fans."

Summer signings starting to settle as rebuild under way

In the summer, Spurs twice broke their transfer record with three of their first signings, as they added centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton , Fernandes from West Ham and Sandro Tonali from Newcastle .

And all three impressed De Zerbi against Chelsea as he added: "Jan Paul van Hecke played very well, Matheus Fernandes played very well, Sandro Tonali played very well.

"I think it was Tonali's best game since joining Tottenham . Omar Marmoush played a good game. It was a tough game for him, but he fought in the right way.

"Mathys Tel played very well too. I think we won the game with our two wingers, Mohammed Kudus and Mathys Tel. They made the difference."

It was notable Fernandes, 22, was criticised by his manager last month.

The return of Maddison, who missed almost all of last season with a serious knee injury, was key in Monday's 3-1 home victory over Coventry City - and he again looked impressive before being withdrawn in the second half with a suspected groin injury.

"I don't think it is a very important problem," said De Zerbi. "I hope it is not a big problem. He is a special player for us. We need him."

Maddison is part of a returning group of players, including Kudus and Dejan Kulusevski, who are making comebacks from lengthy absences.

Spurs are now unbeaten in three games, with back-to-back victories following the 1-1 draw at Manchester United in which they were arguably the better side.

As well as the team meeting before the Old Trafford encounter, Spurs enjoyed a warm-weather training camp in Marbella, where heavyweight boxer Anthony Joshua paid them a visit.

It feels as though some semblance of the old Spurs is returning, although they remain unconvincing in attack with just eight goals in as many games.

Manchester City loanee Marmoush misfired again and his replacement Dominic Solanke was underwhelming in previous matches, while Richarlison has been frozen out in the reserves after being left out of their Premier League squad.

But after this notable derby victory at Chelsea - earning a clean sheet there too for the first time since 1986 - it felt like the first part of De Zerbi's rebuild is well under way.

articles.title: Julián pide perdón: "Mis palabras fueron una equivocación; entiendo a la gente..."
articles.standfirst: El argentino se disculpa por el culebrón del verano
articles.summary: El argentino se disculpa por el culebrón del verano
articles.body: Y Julián Alvarez pidió perdón a la afición del Atlético justo tras su primer gol en el Metropolitano. Una semana redonda para el argentino, que rompió su sequía en Stuttgart antes de marcar en el estadio de una afición que le ovacionó tras el 1-0 que acabó siendo decisivo. "Quería pedir perdón a nuestra gente por mis palabras durante el Mundial. Fueron una equivocación. Las formas y el momento. Sobre todo porque entiendo el enojo de la gente. Yo también me hubiera enojado si fuera hincha. Y más por cómo me han bancado. Fueron muy generosos y eso lo valoro mucho. También quiero agradecer al equipo porque me apoyaron durante este tiempo". Momento: "Me voy sintiendo bien. Agradezco a todos mis compañeros porque me han apoyado. Estoy trabajando para mejorar. Me siento mejor en los últimos partidos. Tanto físicamente como con la pelota. Ayudar al equipo y dar lo mejor". Reflexión: "Cuando uno se siente bien en la vida se ve reflejado en el campo. Si bien somos profesionales. Todo influye. Me siento bien y preparado para competir por todo". Futuro: "Ojalá que con trabajo y humildad pueda revertir esta situación". Más tarde, en los micrófonos de Movistar y luego en rueda de prensa, Simeone agradeció las disculpas de Julián, del que habló muy bien: "Yo valoro mucho de las personas el momento de pedir perdón porque no es fácil. Julián es un chico humilde, trabajador, que quiere a sus compañeros y agradezco su perdón porque lo posiciona en el lugar que él es".

articles.body:
Malachi Toney and Darian Mensah continued their respective Heisman campaigns by leading No. 1 Miami to a blowout of Pitt on Saturday.

Mensah threw for 387 yards with four touchdowns and no picks, while Toney racked up a school-record 16 catches for 194 yards and three scores in the Hurricanes' 52-23 victory.

Here's a look at the top Heisman Trophy odds heading into Week 8 of the 2026 season, courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook .

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State (+8000)

Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith still sits atop the Heisman odds during the Buckeyes' bye week, but his campaign hit a snag when starting quarterback Julian Sayin suffered a potentially season-ending injury last weekend.

Whether Luke Fahey or Tavien St. Clair wins the QB1 battle at Ohio State will shape both the Buckeyes' playoff odds and Smith's odds of being celebrated as the top player in college football.

Oregon State wideout Jesse Legree, who currently leads all college wideouts with 1,040 receiving yards and 14 touchdowns in seven games, is on a bye this weekend.

Georgia and Notre Dame are also on break. Fighting Irish quarterback CJ Carr has retained high odds despite conceding a narrow loss to Bear Bachmeier and BYU last Saturday, while Gunner Stockton remained in the Heisman conversation despite Auburn's upset of Georgia the same day.

Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss will get the chance to build his own case in a Saturday matchup at No. 19 Texas, where Arch Manning has gone from being seen as a Heisman contender to drawing doubts as to his QB1 status going forward.

Joining Manning as an early-season favorite no longer seen as top Heisman candidate is Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover, who struggled in a low-scoring Saturday overtime win at Michigan.

articles.title: Angel Reese, Kaila Charles shine in Game 4 tunnel for WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Sets appeared to be the fashion statement for Game 4 of the WNBA Finals. Angel Reese went schoolgirl chic and Te-Hina Paopao was red hot.
articles.body:
The Golden State Valkyries rebounded in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals and beat the Atlanta Dream 67-62 to go back to Ballhalla flying high.

But neither team has missed a beat in the tunnel. For the second game in Atlanta, both the Valkyries and Dream showed out. It seemed that sets were the fashion statement of this matchup. Naz Hillmon, DeWanna Bonner and Angel Reese wore outfits that featured matching tops and bottoms. But Te-Hina Paopao stole the show in a bold color.

Big Boi, who performed at halftime , put his hat in the ring for the style competition of the game. He wore a luxe brown fur coat and Sleepy Brown wore a similar gray one as they performed a series of OutKast hits (sans André 3000) to get the Atlanta crowd hyped.

Golden State Valkyries, Atlanta Dream battle in WNBA Finals Game 4

Here's the best looks of the WNBA Finals Game 4:

Naz Hillmon looked sharp in an all black fit. She wore a satin cargo jacket and shorts set and her slouchy boots were super fly.

Kaila Charles was on point, letting high-heeled ballet slippers be the statement piece of her outfit. The ruffles on her black shorts added an extra feminine flair.

DeWanna Bonner was fantastic in a brown leather jacket and skirt set. The rimless shades and metallic pumps were superb accessories.

Miela Sowah was sporty in this look. She showed support for FC Barcelona in the soccer club's El Clasico rivalry against Real Madrid this weekend. The kit is from the club's collaboration with Travis Scott and she put it with well-fitting khaki trousers and pumps.

Angel Reese went schoolgirl chic. She wore a red tweed jacket and skirt set. Accessorizing it with a wide headband and Chanel purse completed the look perfectly.

Tiffany Hayes was battle ready in incredible patchwork jeans and a button-up from BAPE's collaboration with Dover Street Market Ginza. Her coolness factor is off the charts.

You can NOT miss Te-Hina Paopao! She drew all the attention in this bright orange jacket and cargo pants set styled by Blvk Indigo . The matching sneakers made this look red hot.

articles.title: Man Utd not an unmanageable club says boss Michael Carrick
articles.summary: Michael Carrick says it is possible to manage Manchester United effectively as he clings on to his job with Bournemouth visiting Old Trafford on Sunday.
articles.body:
Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has dismissed a theory the Old Trafford club are unmanageable.

Carrick is clinging on to his job after a desperate run of seven games without a win before Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth (14:00 GMT).

The pressure on him has been heightened by controversial comments from senior players Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes attacking the club's recruitment and his tactics.

If Carrick were to lose his job, it would be the third change of manager in as many seasons and mean eight long-term bosses, including Ralf Rangnick, have lost their jobs after failing to get close to the heights of Sir Alex Ferguson, who retired in 2013.

Given the pressure on the club is heightened by the number of prominent ex-players who have their own media outlets, and the proliferation of fan channels that attract large numbers of viewers, there is an argument it makes United an impossible club to manage.

Carrick had a one-word answer to that notion: "No."

However, Carrick does take issue with some of the claims made about his team by former professionals and casual observers.

He is vexed at the sense his team do not run enough, and do not press the opposition when they are out of possession.

Carrick has accepted the general performance of his team in a 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como on Wednesday was "unacceptable".

However, he does not see how claims his team do not press stand up to much scrutiny.

"You've got to be careful with just saying 'not running'," he said.

"We've won a lot of games over a period of time and this pressing thing; pressing is one small part of football.

"There are all sorts of different ways that are classed as a press. What actually is it? What are you doing it for? Is it to your strength? Is it covering up other spaces?

"It's just thrown about as a bit of a word at the minute. You don't necessarily need to press to win games of football. Sometimes you do, sometimes you don't.

"It's not necessarily just running stats that define football games either.

"We've just got to get back to doing a lot of the things that we were doing last season and for certain parts of this season."

Although Carrick was appointed ahead of his former boss and team-mate Ole Gunnar Solskjaer as Ruben Amorim's replacement in January, the pair remain close.

Solskjaer drove up to United's base in Trondheim before the pre-season victory over Rosenborg in July to spend time with Carrick and his backroom team.

They have been in touch this week, with Carrick also confirming he had spoken to Ferguson, who is a regular at matches as he approaches his 85th birthday.

Ferguson signed Carrick from Tottenham in 2006 and also managed the midfielder's Manchester United team in his testimonial game at Old Trafford in 2017.

"I speak to both of them quite regularly," he said. "There's nothing particular in that. I'm close to both of them. It's nothing different this week."

Carrick is convinced he can turn the situation around but knows he needs his underperforming squad to deliver against Bournemouth.

"I definitely trust them, 100%," he said.

"We'll be a different team on Sunday. We have to be a different team on Sunday."

articles.title: 49ers star Fred Warner hit with hefty fine as suspension threat looms
articles.summary: The NFL fined 49ers linebacker Fred Warner $65,673. Warner was pegged for two unnecessary roughness violations during San Francisco’s win over the Commanders...
articles.body:
The NFL fined 49ers linebacker Fred Warner $65,673.

Warner was pegged for two unnecessary roughness violations during San Francisco's win over the Commanders last week . Warner was fined $47,762 for a hit on Commanders tight end Chig Okonkwo, where officials threw a flag on the play, but then picked it up.

Warner faces a one-game suspension if he disciplined for two more hits on defenseless players. The 49ers star has also been fined for a hip-drop tackle, which also leads to a potential suspension if he racks up a total of three.

In Week 3, Warner was fined $41,793 for two violations against Cardinals tight end Trey McBride, one penalty being illegal use of the helmet and the other being a hip-drop tackle that went uncalled.

The 49ers nearly blew a 20-point lead against the Commanders on Monday Night Football, but the squad held on for a nail-biting 23-17 win. San Francisco remains unscathed through six weeks of the NFL season, but injuries have already become an issue for the 49ers.

The 49ers will be without their top two wide receivers as Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel are both sidelined. The 6-0 team simply can't afford to lose other stars like Warner because of a suspension.

While the 49ers are undefeated, the NFC West is a loaded division and every loss decreases San Francisco's chances of making a deep playoff run.

articles.title: Burnley sack boss Nicky Hayen amid threat of back-to-back relegations
articles.summary: The Clarets, relegated from the Premier League last season, have won only one of their 12 league games under former Genk boss Hayen
articles.body:
Burnley have sacked head coach Nicky Hayen after just over three months in charge following their 4-1 Sky Bet Championship defeat at Lincoln.

The Clarets, relegated from the Premier League last season, have won only one of their 12 league games under former Genk boss Hayen, 46, who was appointed in July as a replacement for Scott Parker.

A brief statement on the club's official website read: "Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect.

"The Board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season."

The Clarets' loss at Lincoln was their sixth in the league this season and has left them third from bottom in the table, three points from safety.

Belgian Hayen was named as Parker's successor after Burnley had failed to land Wales boss Craig Bellamy and former Wolves manager Rob Edwards.

Hayen had earlier said in his post-match press conference, before news of his dismissal emerged: "It's frustrating for everyone, especially the fans. I want to apologise to them, but I know it doesn't matter because it's another hard defeat for them and I can understand their criticism.

"We haven't got the results. I will keep on working hard as long as I have the chance. But there will be a day if it carries on like this that it stops.

"I don't know (if I will still be in charge). I know it's a really tough defeat and something to think about for the board."

articles.title: USMNT defender Alex Freeman scores first Villarreal goal in comeback win
articles.summary: Alex Freeman scored his first goal for Villarreal on Saturday, Oct. 24, heading home in the second half to spark a 2-1 comeback win against Valencia.
articles.body:
Alex Freeman scored his first goal for Villarreal on Saturday, Oct. 24, heading home in the second half to spark a 2-1 comeback win against Valencia at Mestalla.

Villarreal went down a goal in the first half, but Freeman's header in the 69th minute leveled the match.

The two sides then traded red cards, first Villarreal's Pape Gueye in the 79th minute and then Valencia's Harvey Elliott 10 minutes later. With both sides down to 10 men, Georges Mikautadze found a winner six minutes into stoppage time to seal all three points for the visitors.

The goal continued Freeman's rapid rise for club and country, with the 22-year-old now starting the past five league matches for Villarreal.

Freeman moved to the Yellow Submarine in January after a breakout 2025 campaign with Orlando City in MLS.

The defender has become an ever-present for the U.S. men's national team in the past 18 months, having played in 25 straight matches for Mauricio Pochettino's team. He started four of the USMNT's five World Cup games this summer, scoring against Australia.

USMNT shines in September-October international window

Villarreal coach full of praise for Freeman

In his post-match press conference on Saturday, Villarreal coach Íñigo Pérez had high praise for the 22-year-old American.

"Alex is a super player," Pérez said in Spanish . "He can easily play center back, fullback, left back, further forward, wingback; he's also played on both sides with his national team.

"That versatility and dynamism, combined with his level, give a coach the confidence to play him in any position or ask certain things of him that might surprise him. It allows me to be more courageous.

"As you saw, he's capable of playing with astonishing calmness."

Freeman started at left back at Valencia instead of his typical right-sided defensive spot. Pérez said he trusted Freeman to deal with the pace of Valencia winger David Otorbi.

"Otorbi is very fast, very direct, and Freeman has the ability to contain those types of wingers," Pérez said.

articles.title: Marist football bows to St. Thomas, falls into tie for first place
articles.summary: Marist football was handed a 35-13 home loss by St. Thomas in a Pioneer Football League game in Poughkeepsie on Oct. 24, 2026.
articles.body:
PHOTOS: Marist football hosts St. Thomas

It's a painful time for reflection for Marist football.

The Red Foxes had an opportunity to stretch their lead in the Pioneer Football League but ended up struggling in a 35-13 setback to St. Thomas at Tenney Stadium on Saturday, October 24.

Now Marist (4-4) is mired in a four-way tie for first place, with the visiting Tommies (6-2) joining the Red Foxes, Butler and Dayton at 3-1.

Leading 7-0 after one quarter, Marist gave up 21 second-quarter points to St. Thomas to head into half trailing 21-10. Following a scoreless third, the Tommies posted a pair of touchdowns in the fourth quarter to keep the Red Foxes at bay.

"Disappointed with the result,'' said Marist head coach Mike Willis. "Anytime you see the scoreboard light up this way, you first have to examine what you could have done differently with your players. ... My impression is that we played very hard. We'll evaluate our effort first, and then our technique.''

In a matchup of one of the top offenses in the PFL in St. Thomas and one of the top defenses in Marist, the Tommies won decisively. St. Thomas amassed 429 yards of offense, with 190 through the air on 17-for-25 passing by freshman QB Nick Peipert and 12 more yards by Pierce McCrary. The tall Peipert often got the Tommies out of trouble with his 18 carries and 85 yards.

Marist was held to 57 yards rushing, and starting QB Sonny Mannino was 13-for-25 for 193 yards, throwing a first-quarter 22-yard score to Jayden Taylor (five grabs, 91 yards). Luke Stenson booted field goals of 36 yards in the second quarter and 45 in the fourth.

St. Thomas produced five touchdowns on nine full drives. Marist was forced to punt three times, fumbled the ball away twice and Mannino was picked once (he was also sacked three times). The Tommies held the ball for nearly 39 minutes.

Marist's Jace Williamson and Chase Hatton each had 10 tackles, with eight coming from Tyrell Powell, Kade Wermer and Naheem Ridore. There were no sacks.

Marist is 0-6 against St. Thomas, coming off a 45-0 loss in St. Paul, Minnesota, in 2025.

Marist heads to San Diego for a 4 p.m. contest on October 31. The Red Foxes close with Morehead State on Nov. 7, Butler on Nov. 14 and Davidson on the road on Nov. 21.

articles.title: Oregon's College Football Playoff hopes get extinguished with 21-10 loss at Illinois
articles.summary: The Ducks have three losses. And a playoff path looks virtually impossible.
articles.body:
Oregon's 2026 season is quickly becoming a disaster.

Any hope of the Ducks sneaking into the College Football Playoff with a streak of late-season wins likely disappeared with a 21-10 loss to an Illinois team that was missing starting quarterback Katin Houser.

Freshman Michael Clayton II started in Houser's place and found Collin Dixon for the game-sealing touchdown with less than three minutes to go.

It was a fantastic juggling catch by Dixon, who got control of the ball before he hit the ground. Oregon (4-3) played its third straight game without starting quarterback Dante Moore after his concussion against USC. The Ducks were also missing four of their top five wide receivers due to injury.

But this is also an Oregon team that was built for a national title run and was the AP's preseason No. 2; the Ducks should have the depth to win a game on the road like this. Former five-star recruit Dylan Raiola transferred from Nebraska and entered the season as Moore's backup after two years as the Huskers' starter.

He played so poorly in the Ducks' loss to UCLA that he didn't start in Week 7 against Nebraska, though he entered the game for Brock Thomas in the second half and led Oregon on its game-winning drive.

Saturday, Oregon's downfield passing attack was nonexistent until it was desperation time. That was against an Illinois defense that was so bad to start the season that it parted ways with first-year coordinator (and former Montana head coach) Bobby Hauck just four games into the season.

Raiola finished the game 27-of-41 passing for 246 yards. That yardage total was padded by a 36-yard desperation completion as time expired.

Entering Week 8, there was a reason to think Oregon could make a playoff push. Moore's return to the field appeared closer and closer, and the schedule looked far more appealing than it once did thanks to Ohio State QB Julian Sayin's injury.

A win in Columbus on Nov. 7 could have been a springboard to another Big Ten title game appearance with the uncertainty across the conference and the down years by schools like Michigan and Penn State, among others.

After all, this was a roster that not only returned Moore, but brought back a lot of talent along the defensive line and added Minnesota safety Koi Perich to the secondary. The running back room was deep, and Jamari Johnson was primed for a bigger role following Kenyon Sadiq's departure.

Instead, Oregon looks like a team that could drop below .500 with No. 24 Northwestern coming to Eugene ahead of that trip to Ohio State.

No matter if Moore is back or not, there's a lot to figure out for Oregon coach Dan Lanning. The Ducks were beaten with Moore on the field in Week 2 at Oklahoma State. That was a game where the stances of Oregon's offensive linemen appeared to reveal what type of play the Ducks would run.

Outside of a Week 4 win at USC, it's been a sloppy, sloppy season. And one that's likely to end with an appearance in a game like the Holiday Bowl instead of with the national title on the line.

articles.title: NC State fires head coach Dave Doeren following 3-4 start, Todd Goebbel to serve as interim
articles.summary: Doeren had been the head coach at NC State since 2013.
articles.body:
NC State has fired head coach Dave Doeren , the school announced on Saturday evening.

Doeren led the Wolfpack to a 3-4 start to the season and most recently lost to Stanford 31-28 on Friday night. He had three years left on his deal, and ESPN's Pete Thamel reports that he is still owed about $10.3 million.

NC State AD Boo Corrigan released a statement about the decision.

"I want to thank Coach Doeren for his service and contributions to NC State, and for always representing the university with pride," said Corrigan. "I appreciate his leadership during his 14-year tenure and the passion he brought to this role. We wish Dave, Sara and his family the best in the future."

Running backs coach/special teams coordinator Todd Goebbel will serve as the interim head coach for the remainder of the regular season.

NC State hired Doeren as head football coach in 2013 after a two-year stint as head coach at Northern Illinois.

After a 14-year career with the Wolfpack, his tenure ends with a 121-78 overall record, including a 5-6 bowl record.

NC State went 8-5 last season, including a bowl win, but the Wolfpack hadn't won double-digit games in a season during his tenure as head coach.

The season began with a 34-8 loss against Virginia, and the assumption was that the Wolfpack needed to turn things around quick for him to keep his job. After a blowout win over Richmond, NC State made headlines in its third game against Vanderbilt for all the wrong reasons.

That was the game where the Wolfpack had the game won, up three, and the Commodores had no timeouts with six seconds left. NC State was in its own end zone, and all quarterback CJ Bailey had to do was not fumble. Even a safety wouldn't hurt on its own.

Bailey appeared to panic and fumbled while trying to go down to the ground. Vanderbilt recovered the ball in the end zone for the surprise win.

NC State bounced back with wins over App State and Louisville. The Wolfpack then lost to Wake Forest before a bye week. NC State went on the road to play Stanford on Friday night and lost 31-28 to the Cardinal.

Goebbel takes over a 3-4 squad with five games to go. NC State still has games against Cal, Duke, Syracuse and Florida State before its rivalry game against North Carolina.

The Wolfpack need to win three of their remaining games to be bowl-eligible. NC State hasn't not qualified for a bowl game since 2019. The Wolfpack didn't play one in 2021, but that was because their game against UCLA was canceled after the Bruins pulled out hours before kickoff due to COVID-19 protocols.

articles.title: CFB Playoff Picture, Standings and Bracket Predictions After Week 8 of 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: The Big 12 turned into the center of the college football universe on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Big 12 turned into the center of the college football universe on Saturday.

The second-ranked BYU Cougars fell in double overtime in Orlando to the UCF Knights, one week after they shocked the college football world with a win over the Notre Dame Fighting Irish.

BYU will fall back from its No. 2 spot in the AP Top 25, but the win over Notre Dame should allow the Cougars to remain in a comfortable College Football Playoff position.

Prior to the chaos in Orlando, the No. 8 Texas Tech Red Raiders fell on the road against the Cincinnati Bearcats.

Texas Tech's first loss of the 2026 season will likely take it out of the projected 12-team playoff field when the new AP Top 25 comes out on Sunday.

There's still more drama to come in the Big 12, as the No. 10 Utah Utes play host to the No. 14 Houston Cougars in what was billed as the game of the week going into Saturday.

The SEC was not to be outdone, though, because the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels and No. 11 Tennessee Volunteers suffered their second defeats on Saturday.

After Week 8, only the Georgia Bulldogs and Kentucky Wildcats have fewer than two total losses in the SEC.

No. 2 BYU Upset By UCF In Double Overtime

BYU's reign as the No. 2 team in the country lasted one whole week.

The Cougars dropped their first game of the season in double overtime to the UCF Knights.

BYU failed to answer UCF's touchdown and two-point conversion in the second overtime period. The Cougars didn't create much separation from their Big 12 foe all afternoon long.

The question now around BYU is how many spots it will fall in the AP Top 25.

BYU still has a win over Notre Dame to hang its hat on, so it won't experience a terrible drop, but it will be penalized for its defeat in Orlando.

A place in the top four may seem unlikely after the loss, but BYU still has plenty to play for in the Big 12.

Texas Tech lost on Saturday, and even if Utah beats Houston, the Cougars have a shot at the Utes on November 7. There's the potential for all three of the Big 12's best teams to have one loss.

If BYU beats Utah, it would hold a pair of ranked wins that neither of its closest competitors in the Big 12 possess. That could be a huge difference-maker down the road for BYU.

For now, the Cougars just have to try and rebound at home in Week 9 against the Arizona State Sun Devils.

Texas Tech struggled on the road in Cincinnati on Saturday afternoon, a loss that will more than likely drop them to the fringe of the top 15, or out of it entirely.

The good news for the Red Raiders is that they don't have to play BYU or Utah in the regular season and have one tough road test remaining against the Oklahoma State Cowboys.

They still have a good setup to get into the 12-team playoff field, but like many other teams, the margin for error has diminished significantly.

There's actually a world where Texas Tech would benefit from missing out on the Big 12 Championship Game as a one-loss team so that it can preserve its spot in the field, instead of risking a second loss so late in the season, if that is the scenario in play.

The Tennessee Volunteers were unable to keep the momentum going from last week's win over Alabama.

The Vols fell on a last-second field goal to the South Carolina Gamecocks on the road on Saturday.

The Week 8 loss dropped the Vols to 6-2 and in danger of not being in the playoff conversation for the rest of the season.

Tennessee's loss to the Texas Longhorns in September doesn't look as good as it did back in Week 4. A defeat at the hands of unranked South Carolina won't help the Vols' case either.

Tennessee still has to play the Kentucky Wildcats and LSU Tigers in November, so there is a chance it can still make it into the 12-team field.

However, the Vols are on thin ice and more one defeat likely takes them out of the playoff discussion.

Unranked Teams Cause Chaos in Rankings 📊

No. 7 Ole Miss Loses to Arch Manning and No. 19 Texas

Ole Miss dropped to 5-2 with a loss to Texas.

The Rebels played from behind for most of the night against Arch Manning and the Longhorns.

Trinidad Chambliss and Co. now have one of the weirder resumes among the CFB Playoff contenders.

Ole Miss owns a Week 1 win over the then-No. 25 Louisville Cardinals and a home win over the LSU Tigers, but it fell on the road to Texas and the Florida Gators.

The November 7 clash in Oxford with the Georgia Bulldogs now carries even more importance for Ole Miss because it could be playing for its playoff life in that game.

Texas got off the mat after its two-game losing streak and it is now back in the playoff conversation.

The Longhorns have November road trips to Missouri and LSU, so they aren't in the clear quite yet.

However, with so many SEC teams now with multiple losses, there is a chance Texas gets into the field with two defeats. It could even reach the 12-team field with three losses depending on how the rest of the season shakes out in the SEC.

articles.title: Morera, el 'Ungüento amarillo' que resolvió el primer Clásico
articles.standfirst: Dos goles del canario dieron al Madrid el triunfo en la que era su primera visita en la Liga al campo del Barcelona
articles.summary: Dos goles del canario dieron al Madrid el triunfo en la que era su primera visita en la Liga al campo del Barcelona
articles.body: El término clásico nada tenía que ver con el fútbol el 17 de febrero de 1929. Ese día en Las Corts se jugó un gran partido de fútbol. Sólo, o nada más y nada menos que eso. El Real Madrid visitaba por primera vez en la Liga la casa del Barcelona. Era una rivalidad naciente entre los dos equipos de las dos ciudades más importantes del país. Aquella tarde, el programa fue doble en Las Corts. Porque antes se disputó otro partido de Primera: el Europa, con cuatro goles de Cros, ganó 5-2 al Arenas de Getxo. Acabado ese partido saltaron al campo Barcelona y Madrid, capitaneados por Samitier y Quesada, ordenados por el árbitro guipuzcoano Steinborn y aplaudidos con abundancia ambos equipos. Era solo la segunda jornada de la historia de la Liga. Ese primer enfrentamiento liguero entre culés y merengues tuvo un nombre estelar. Pero es uno de esos que con el paso de los años se ha perdido entre los recodos del tiempo. Dos goles de Rafael Morera dieron al Madrid el triunfo, que hizo pleno en los primeros cinco partidos de una Liga que tuvo al Barcelona como su primer campeón. Para encontrar los orígenes del primer bigoleador en un Clásico hay que viajar primero a Lanzarote, donde nació, y luego a un barrio de Santa Cruz de Tenerife, El Toscal, donde creció. Allí jugaba de extremo izquierdo un muchacho nacido el 12 de noviembre de 1903. Lo hacía en el Recreativo, un modesto equipo que llevaba el nombre de un parque que ya no existe. Del parque pasó al Luz y Vida y a uno de los clubes fundamentales en el desarrollo del fútbol canario: el Iberia. En septiembre de 1922, por iniciativa de unos socios de la Sociedad de Recreo, Instrucción y Fomento del Barrio del Toscal Luz y Vida, nació la entidad desde la que llegaron al Madrid los dos primeros futbolistas canarios de su historia: Paco López y Rafael Morera. Ambos llegaron a la capital de España en 1928. Eran los meses previos al inicio del primer campeonato nacional de Liga. El Madrid fichaba a un jugador que se movía como pez en el agua por la zona izquierda del ataque, fuese como interior o como extremo. Pero encontró a un futbolista capaz de desenvolverse en cualquier posición del terreno de juego. “En el Madrid batí un récord. Me alineé en todos los puestos del equipo, menos de portero. Donde figuraba más frecuentemente era de interior y extremo izquierdo; pero siempre que fuese necesario, allí estaba yo para cubrir cualquier demarcación”, comentaba años después de dejar la Casa Blanca. Eso le valió el apoyo del Ungüento amarillo, la famosa pomada que se utilizaba para curar cualquier herida en animales e incluso humanos. “Este muchacho es como el ungüento amarillo, lo mismo pinta que arregla el tejao, que guisa, que lava la ropa...”, se decía en la época. Pero también tenía su parte irónica: “Eres como el ungüento amarillo, que pa’ todo vale y pa’ nada aprovecha”. No era el caso de Morera. De su etapa en el Madrid, que siempre recordó con cariño, le quedaron tres campeonatos regionales ganados y una final de Copa cargada de historia. Fue la jugada en Mestalla el 3 de febrero de 1929, en un campo que era una enorme balsa de agua. El Espanyol ganó 2-1 al Madrid, pero si el marcador no fue más claro para los catalanes fue por algo que siempre recordó Morera: “Las espectaculares paradas de Zamora”. Eso ocurrió sólo dos semanas antes de que el Madrid apareciera en Las Corts para ganar con los dos goles de Morera. El primero, gracias a un formidable remate al ángulo de Rafael Vidal; el segundo, al aprovechar las manos blandas del meta azulgrana. Eran tres goles en las dos primeras jornadas para el canario. En el 5-1 al Europa en el estreno del Madrid en la Liga, suyo fue el tanto que se sumó a los cuatro de Lazcano. Feliz en Madrid en los casi cuatro años que fue jugador blanco, la selección nunca le llamó, aunque con la militar de Madrid viajó a Lisboa en mayo. Al estar en la lista varios jugadores blancos, se hubo de aplazar el Madrid-Barcelona de Liga, el que sería un 0-1 decisivo para el desenlace del título. En la primavera de 1932 regresó a casa. Se comprometió con el Tenerife para jugar la ronda de dieciseisavos de Copa ante el Betis. Los canarios fueron eliminados (1-1 y 4-1), pero Morera fue jugador del Tenerife durante más de una década. Con más de 40 años fue cuando decidió parar. Entre sus logros aparece la fecha del 18 de marzo de 1934. En la vuelta previa de la Copa, el Tenerife ganó 2-3 en el campo del Hércules. No valió de nada a Morera y sus compañeros, porque en la isla habían perdido 1-4. Pero esa es la primera victoria del Tenerife en una competición nacional. El 29 de abril de 1981 falleció en Tenerife.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Experts Top 25 Rankings After Week 8
articles.summary: Another week, another round of absolute chaos.
articles.body:
Another week, another round of absolute chaos.

With BYU and Texas Tech both suffering their first loss of the season to unranked opponents, the Big 12 race has been turned upside down, and so has the top of the Top 25 rankings.

Tennessee, USC, Iowa and James Madison were also on the wrong end of upset losses, opening the door for multiple newcomers to the Top 25 and further muddying the College Football Playoff picture.

Ahead is an updated look at how the college football experts here at B/R line up the nation's top 25 teams following Week 8 action.

Editor's Note: These rankings will be updated after the conclusion of Houston vs. Utah.

Week 8 Result: WIN at Tulane (42-19) Next Week: BYE

A 30-6 loss to Texas when they were No. 1 in the AP poll is the only blemish on UTSA's resume, and they are steadily playing their way into the Group of Six conversation as they march through AAC play. The rushing attack shouldered the load against Tulane, as they finished with 223 yards and six touchdowns on the ground. If they can run the table over their final four games, they might be the next team up if Boise State falters.

Week 8 Result: LOSS at Wisconsin (7-24) Next Week: vs. Ohio State

The Trojans entered Saturday's game averaging 36.4 points per game as one of the most potent offenses in the country, but they were held to just seven points, the fewest points ever by a Lincoln Riley coached team. They finished with negative-17 rushing yards on 25 carries, and quarterback Jayden Maiava was unable to pick up the slack, completing 31-of-50 pass attempts for 258 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions. Two missed field goals and two turnovers on downs was all they produced after halftime.

Week 8 Result: WIN vs. USC (24-7) Next Week: at Iowa

A stout Wisconsin defense entered Saturday's game allowing just 16.7 points per game, and they put together a dominant performance against a high-powered USC offense. The Trojans finished with negative-17 rushing yards and turned it over twice to go along with two turnovers on downs, and that was enough for the Badgers to cruise to victory despite just 200 total yards and 58 passing yards. Who's ready for an ugly one next weekend against Iowa?

Full details following the conclusion of tonight's game.

21. Northwestern (6-1, Previous Rank: 24)

Week 8 Result: WIN vs. Rutgers (42-14) Next Week: at Oregon

Aidan Chiles had 219 passing yards, 83 rushing yards and five total touchdowns in a dominant victory, and Northwestern is 6-1 for the first time since the abridged 2020 season. The Wildcats' schedule gets significantly more difficult going forward with Oregon, Iowa and Ohio State on the calendar the next three weeks, but they have been one of college football's biggest surprises after being picked to finish 14th in the Big Ten's preseason media poll.

Week 8 Result: BYE Next Week: at Georgia

The Gators have top-10 wins over Ole Miss and Texas sandwiched around a two-game losing streak against Missouri and South Carolina, making them one of the tougher teams to nail down. Next week's matchup with Georgia will be a major test, and they will need a big performance from star running back Jadan Baugh (135 carries, 763 yards, 13 TD) against a Bulldogs defense that allowed just 91.4 rushing yards per game.

Week 8 Result: LOSS at Cincinnati (24-37) Next Week: vs. Arizona

The Red Raiders had three turnovers, three punts, a turnover on downs and a missed field goal, and that was ultimately too many empty possessions for them to overcome a Cincinnati offense that had four passing touchdowns and 255 rushing yards. Will Hammond (24/37, 227 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT) had an inefficient day through the air, lost a fumble and managed just 23 rushing yards on 14 carries. Next week's matchup with Arizona now becomes a must-win for Texas Tech if they are going to stay alive in the playoff picture.

Week 8 Result: WIN vs. California (59-20) Next Week: at Syracuse

Kevin Jennings became SMU's all-time leader in passing touchdowns when he connected with Derek McFall in the third quarter, surpassing Tanner Mordecai on the all-time leaderboard, and he is already the school's leader in completions and passing yards. The Mustangs actually trailed 20-17 at halftime, but scored 42 unanswered points after halftime to come away with the blowout win and improve to 4-1 in ACC play.

17. Boise State (6-1, Previous Rank: 21)

Week 8 Result: WIN at Washington State (31-10) Next Week: vs. Texas State

The Broncos scored 21 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to turn a 10-10 game into a lopsided victory, starting with a 10-play, 70-yard drive that chewed more than seven minutes off the clock. A staggering 258-53 advantage in rushing yardage was the story of the game, as Boise State allowed just 1.6 yards per carry and dominated the line of scrimmage. That run defense will be put to the test next weekend when Pac-12 leading rusher Torrance Burgess Jr. and Texas State come to town.

16. Wake Forest (6-1, Previous Rank: 18)

Week 8 Result: BYE Next Week: vs. Virginia

Ranked in the AP Top 25 for the first time since 2022, the Demon Deacons' playoff outlook might boil down to who comes out on top in their Nov. 14 matchup with SMU. North Carolina transfer Gio Lopez has been one of this season's biggest breakout quarterbacks, leading the ACC in total yards (2,200) and total touchdowns (23) to help Wake Forest average 37.4 points per game.

Week 8 Result: WIN vs. Iowa State (39-3) Next Week: at Texas Tech

Noah Fifita and the Arizona offense have been the story for much of the season, but it was the Wildcats' defense that turned in a dominant performance in Week 8. The Cyclones kicked a field goal on their second drive of the game and didn't put points on the board the rest of the way, with 80 of their 221 total yards coming on that one scoring drive. Fifita (27/34, 308 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT) had another efficient performance under center, while Isaiah Mizell (8 catches, 134 yards, 1 TD) had his second straight 100-yard receiving game.

Week 8 Result: LOSS at Texas (27-34) Next Week: vs. Auburn

The Rebels battled back after falling behind 24-3 in the first half, but their comeback bid ultimately fell short as Trinidad Chambliss' third interception of the game came on a Hail Mary heave as time expired. The Texas secondary limited Chambliss to 25-of-52 passing and had eight pass deflections to go along with the three interceptions, and with running back Kewan Lacy (16 carries, 36 yards) held in check that was the story of the game.

Week 8 Result: WIN vs. Ole Miss (34-27) Next Week: vs. Mississippi State

The Texas defense held strong against Ole Miss star Trinidad Chambliss on the final drive of the game to halt any potential heroics, and for the fifth time in seven games the outcome of a Longhorns game was seven points or fewer. It looked like things were headed for a more lopsided finish when they built a 24-3 halftime lead, but the Rebels stormed back. Arch Manning had a passing touchdown and two rushing touchdowns, but also turned it over three times in another uneven performance.

Week 8 Result: WIN vs. Texas A&M (31-20) Next Week: BYE

Keelon Russell had 311 passing yards and three touchdowns, including a pair of fourth-quarter strikes to flip a 20-17 deficit into a 31-20 victory. The Crimson Tide managed just 68 rushing yards, which put more pressure on Russell's arm to shoulder the offensive load, and he stepped up to help avoid a potentially devastating third loss. They get a bye next week before what could amount to a playoff elimination game with fellow two-loss SEC contender LSU on Nov. 7.

Week 8 Result: LOSS at South Carolina (24-27) Next Week: BYE

The Volunteers had a 24-17 lead and the football with 8:13 remaining, and while they ran plenty of clock with a nine-play, 59-yard drive, they ultimately turned it over on downs. South Carolina seized that opportunity with a touchdown drive that tied the game with 1:17 remaining, and a fumble by Tennessee quarterback George MacIntyre gave the Gamecocks the ball back with enough time to kick the game-winning field goal. Workhorse running back DeSean Bishop (32 carries, 120 yards, 1 TD) was held to 3.8 yards per carry, well below his 6.0 season average.

Week 8 Result: WIN at Auburn (38-17) Next Week: BYE

The Tigers had four first-half touchdowns to build a 31-10 halftime lead, taking care of business against an Auburn team coming off a huge win against Georgia a week ago. Sam Leavitt (32/45, 387 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT, 1 rush TD) had a huge game on the offensive side of the ball, while the LSU defense did a great job limiting dual-threat quarterback Byrum Brown to 181 total yards and one touchdown while surrendering 1.9 yards per carry. With Alabama, Texas and Tennessee up next after the bye week, the SEC gauntlet continues.

Week 8 Result: WIN vs. Vanderbilt (34-17) Next Week: BYE

The Wildcats are 7-1 for the first time since 2018 when they finished 10-3 and won the Citrus Bowl, and now they get a week to rest before a three-week stretch against Tennessee, Florida and Missouri that will ultimately determine the ceiling of their season. Kenny Minchey had 203 passing yards, 23 rushing yards and two touchdowns as he continues to be one of the bigger breakout stories in the SEC this year after transferring from Notre Dame.

A one-loss Notre Dame team still fits comfortably into the projected College Football Playoff field, especially considering that loss came against another playoff-caliber opponent in BYU, but their margin for error the rest of the way has shrunk considerably. They have home games against Miami (Nov. 7) and SMU (Nov. 21) to navigate. Losing one of those would put them squarely on the bubble, and losing both would likely eliminate them from consideration for a spot in the 12-team field.

Week 8 Result: WIN vs. Michigan State (28-10) Next Week: vs. Nevada

The Bruins defense allowed just 156 total yards, forced seven punts and had three takeaways, stifling a Michigan State team that is still searching for its first Big Ten conference win. Anthony Woods (14 carries, 112 yards, 1 TD) anchored a rushing attack that piled up 48 carries for 245 yards and three touchdowns, and UCLA is 7-0 for the first time since 2005. The only ranked team left on their schedule is the regular-season finale against USC, so this team is a legitimate candidate to crash the playoff picture.

Week 8 Result: LOSS at UCF (31-39, 2OT) Next Week: vs. Arizona State

Fresh off one of the biggest wins in school history last week against Notre Dame, the Cougars crashed back to earth with a double-overtime loss to a 4-3 UCF team. They went three-and-out twice in the fourth quarter with the game tied, and needed a blocked field goal to force overtime. The defense couldn't come up with a stop on either of UCF's overtime possessions, and Bear Bachemier threw three straight incompletions from the UCF 4-yard line to end the game. They still have a strong one-loss resume, but the Nov. 7 matchup with Utah might now be a must-win game if they want to be part of the playoff picture.

Week 8 Result: vs. Houston Next Week: at Cincinnati

4. Indiana Hoosiers (7-1, Previous Rank: 5)

Week 8 Result: WIN at Michigan (13-6, OT) Next Week: vs. Minnesota

Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover completed his first pass since the second quarter when he connected with Brock Schott for 21 yards to begin overtime. He then scored on a keeper on the next play and the Indiana defense held on Michigan's ensuing possession to avoid the upset.

The Indiana offense finished with just 11 first downs against seven punts, with Hoover completing 8-of-18 pass attempts for 81 yards and an interception, but the defense was able to carry the day.

The Wolverines' rushing attack was bottled up for just 57 yards on 42 carries, and that forced true freshman quarterback Tommy Carr to attempt 32 passes while averaging just 5.2 yards per attempt. It wasn't pretty, but road wins in the Big House are never easy.

3. Georgia Bulldogs (6-1, Previous Rank: 4)

Week 8 Result: BYE Next Week: vs. Florida

After suffering their first loss of the season at home against Auburn in Week 7, the Bulldogs get a week to regroup and for what will be a grueling stretch of games on the other side of their bye.

Florida, Ole Miss and Missouri are on deck the next three weekends, and they will almost certainly need to go at least 2-1 in those games to stay in the projected College Football Playoff field.

Through seven weeks, quarterback Gunner Stockton led the SEC in completion percentage (74.1), yards per attempt (9.9) and passer rating (185.9), though he will need to bounce back from a three-turnover performance in the loss to Auburn.

2. Ohio State Buckeyes (6-1, Previous Rank: 3)

The Buckeyes have won five straight since their Week 2 loss to Texas, outscoring the opposition 196-67 during that stretch while picking up road wins over Iowa and Indiana to solidify their College Football Playoff resume.

Star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (52 catches, 984 yards, 12 TD) is the Heisman Trophy betting favorite entering Week 8, while quarterback Julian Sayin entered this week's action leading the Big Ten in passing touchdowns (19), yards per attempt (10.5) and passer rating (184.5).

However, Sayin is sidelined indefinitely and could miss the rest of the season after suffering an injury to his throwing arm in Week 7 that saw him end the game with his arm in a sling on the sidelines. Can true freshman Luke Fahey or sophomore Tavien St. Clair pick up the slack in his absence?

1. Miami Hurricanes (7-0, Previous Rank: 1)

Week 8 Result: WIN vs. Pittsburgh (52-23) Next Week: at North Carolina

The Hurricanes built a 17-0 lead early and opened things up to 38-7 when they scored on the opening drive of the second half before cruising to victory to improve to 5-0 in ACC play and stay undefeated on the year.

The Pitt defense had no answer for the Darian Mensah (31/37, 387 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT) and Malachi Toney (16 catches, 194 yards, 3 TD) connection, while the Hurricanes rushing attack combined for 119 yards and three scores to help pile on in the lopsided win.

An upset-minded North Carolina team awaits next weekend in what looks like a classic trap game ahead of the high-profile showdown with Notre Dame on Nov. 7.

Others receiving votes: Cincinnati, Iowa

articles.title: Wisconsin makes noise with upset win over USC
articles.summary: Wisconsin football once faced hot seat concerns for head coach Luke Fickell. Now the Badgers coach helped put USC coach Lincoln Riley there. All thanks to W...
articles.body:
Wisconsin football once faced hot seat concerns for head coach Luke Fickell . Now the Badgers coach helped put USC coach Lincoln Riley there. All thanks to Wisconsin trouncing the No. 16 Trojans 24-7 in Madison Saturday.

The fans flooded the field at Madison after watching their team pull off the latest top 25 upset on a wild Oct. 24.

USC joined No. 2 BYU, No. 8 Texas Tech, No. 11 Tennessee and No. 15 Iowa in losing during the same weekend. But Wisconsin delivered its first statement win in the era of Fickell.

The former Cincinnati coach once came in decorated with a past College Football Playoff resume. He even left the Bearcats during a time they transitioned to the Big 12 Conference. But now Fickell pulled off an epic masterclass of coaching by pivoting back to past Badgers tactics.

Wisconsin battered USC with its ground game, tallying 142 rushing yards there. The Badgers then delivered five sacks of USC quarterback Jayden Maiava , including intercepting him twice. Wisconsin turned to defense, ball control and owning the line of scrimmage to pull off this upset. These tactics turned the Badgers into a Rose Bowl and Cotton Bowl contender under past coaches Barry Alvarez, Bret Bielema, then Paul Chryst.

So the Badgers now will more than likely garner top 25 attention. Meanwhile, USC legend Keyshawn Johnson called out Riley following the rough loss , saying "it ain't working out" and "tough decisions must be made."

USC's remaining schedule doesn't lighten either. The Trojans face three teams ranked in the top 10 (Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA) still.
